title: UAV3DCrop: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction in Repeated Multi-Angle UAV Crop Surveys
comment: 22 pages, 7 figures. Dataset and project page: https://link-dev.github.io/UAV3DCrop/
summary: Accurate 3D crop monitoring underpins data-driven precision agriculture by enabling field-scale analysis of plant structure, growth dynamics, and management response. Modern 3D reconstruction methods perform strongly on generic benchmarks, but rendered appearance may not translate into metrically and agronomically useful geometry in crop fields. We introduce UAV3DCrop, a public benchmark of repeated multi-angle unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) crop surveys. It contains 88,830 RGB images at $5280 \times 3956$ pixels, with a ground sampling distance of 3.6-5.8 mm, from 91 scenes spanning corn, soybean, wheat, and oat. Track A evaluates seven scene-optimized methods -- Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) variants -- on held-out views, photogrammetry-referenced depth, and canopy-height recovery. Track B tests four pretrained feed-forward models on zero-shot camera-pose and geometry estimation. The scene-optimized methods rank differently across the three targets: Splatfacto-big leads appearance, whereas Scaffold-GS leads depth and is statistically tied with Splatfacto for canopy height. Among feed-forward models, MapAnything leads on seven of the eight metrics, while the remaining models vary more across crops and fail severely on absolute scale in a way that alignment conceals. Repeated acquisitions reveal further sensitivities that differ by output type and by model, associated with position within the acquisition sequence and with tie-point multiplicity. Current 3D reconstruction methods are therefore not yet interchangeable for agronomic use: no single method wins on appearance, geometry, and canopy height at once, and only one of four feed-forward models recovers usable metric scale. The dataset is publicly available at https://link-dev.github.io/UAV3DCrop/

AI.tldr: This paper introduces UAV3DCrop, a public benchmark dataset of 88,830 high-resolution UAV images from 91 crop scenes (corn, soybean, wheat, oat) with repeated multi-angle surveys. It evaluates 3D reconstruction methods across three tracks: appearance, depth/geometry, and canopy-height recovery for scene-optimized methods (NeRF/3DGS variants), plus zero-shot pose and geometry estimation for feed-forward models. Results show no single method wins across all targets—Splatfacto-big leads in appearance, Scaffold-GS leads in depth, and only one of four feed-forward models recovers usable metric scale.
AI.motivation: Modern 3D reconstruction methods perform well on generic benchmarks but may fail to produce metrically and agronomically useful geometry in real crop fields, which are critical for precision agriculture. There is a lack of public benchmarks specifically designed to evaluate 3D reconstruction for agronomic applications with realistic crop survey conditions.
AI.method: The authors construct UAV3DCrop, a benchmark with 88,830 RGB images from 91 scenes spanning four crop types, acquired via repeated multi-angle UAV surveys with ground sampling distance of 3.6-5.8 mm. Track A evaluates seven scene-optimized NeRF and 3DGS variants on held-out views, photogrammetry-referenced depth, and canopy-height recovery. Track B tests four pretrained feed-forward models on zero-shot camera-pose and geometry estimation. The dataset is publicly released.
AI.result: Scene-optimized methods rank differently across targets: Splatfacto-big leads in appearance, Scaffold-GS leads in depth and ties with Splatfacto for canopy height. Among feed-forward models, MapAnything leads on seven of eight metrics, while others vary by crop and fail severely on absolute scale. Repeated acquisitions reveal model- and output-type-specific sensitivities related to acquisition sequence position and tie-point multiplicity.
AI.conclusion: Current 3D reconstruction methods are not yet interchangeable for agronomic use—no single method simultaneously wins on appearance, geometry, and canopy height, and only one of four feed-forward models recovers usable metric scale. This motivates the need for further development of crop-specific 3D reconstruction methods.

title: Deep Evidential Regression for Sparse Forest Height Estimation from Multimodal Satellite Imagery
summary: Accurate estimation of forest height from satellite imagery is essential for applications such as carbon accounting, biodiversity monitoring, and ecosystem management. While recent deep learning approaches provide accurate predictions, they typically do not quantify predictive uncertainty. This limitation is particularly relevant in geospatial settings characterized by sparse supervision and geographic distribution shift. In this work, we investigate Deep Evidential Regression (DER) for forest height estimation on the TreeUQ benchmark, a large-scale dataset designed for the joint estimation of tree count and average tree height at 10 m resolution, based on Sentinel-1/-2 data as well as tree inventory data over the federal state of Bavaria. To account for the extreme label sparsity of the tree inventory data, we introduce a masked evidential loss for dense geospatial prediction. Using a U-Net architecture with multimodal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 inputs, the proposed approach jointly predicts tree height and associated uncertainty estimates in a single forward pass. Experimental results show that DER achieves predictive performance comparable to a deterministic U-Net while additionally providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates. These findings demonstrate the potential of evidential learning as an efficient framework for uncertainty-aware forest structure estimation from Earth observation data.

AI.tldr: This paper applies Deep Evidential Regression (DER) to forest height estimation using a U-Net architecture with multimodal Sentinel-1/-2 inputs on the TreeUQ benchmark, introducing a masked evidential loss to handle extreme label sparsity. The method achieves accuracy comparable to deterministic U-Net while providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates in a single forward pass.
AI.motivation: Forest height estimation is critical for carbon accounting, biodiversity monitoring, and ecosystem management, but deep learning approaches typically lack predictive uncertainty quantification—especially problematic in geospatial settings with sparse supervision and geographic distribution shift.
AI.method: Deep Evidential Regression (DER) with a U-Net architecture, multimodal Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 inputs, and a novel masked evidential loss for dense geospatial prediction that accounts for extreme label sparsity in tree inventory data.
AI.result: DER achieves predictive performance comparable to a deterministic U-Net while additionally providing well-calibrated uncertainty estimates on the TreeUQ benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Evidential learning demonstrates potential as an efficient framework for uncertainty-aware forest structure estimation from Earth observation data.

title: TransSLR: A Lightweight Transformer for Sign Language Recognition
comment: This paper has been accepted for oral presentation at Deep Learning Indaba 2026 which will be hosted on the IJCAI hosting platform. paper link: https://chairingtool.com/conferences/dli2026/main-track/submissions/356
summary:
Automated Sign Language Recognition for under-represented languages remains a largely unsolved problem. Central African Sign Language (CASL) exemplifies this gap: the only available bench-mark, CASL-W60, has a best reported accuracy of 69.93%, and we show that the common heuristic of fine-tuning high-resource models fails to close it. This failure stems from two compounding factors: the limited scale of available CASL data and the significant lexical and visual domain gap between CASL and large-scale corpora such as WLASL, which renders pre-trained representations largely uninformative.
  To address this, we propose TransSLR, a lightweight Temporal Transformer Encoder trained from scratch on 64-frame normalized pose sequences, with average pooling and a classification head. By operating on geometric keypoint representations rather than raw RGB, TransSLR achieves signer-independent generalization without relying on visual appearance. On the CASL-W60 benchmark, TransSLR establishes a new state-of-the-art accuracy of 80.39%, surpassing the prior best by +10.46%. Beyond accuracy, our encoder-only design significantly reduces computational overhead, making deployment feasible in resource-constrained environments. We conduct extensive experiments on the CASL-W60 benchmark, comparing against RGB-based and multimodal baselines, and demonstrate that TransSLR achieves state-of-the-art performance.

AI.tldr: The authors propose TransSLR, a lightweight Temporal Transformer Encoder trained from scratch on pose sequences for Central African Sign Language (CASL) recognition, achieving 80.39% accuracy on CASL-W60 — a +10.46% improvement over the prior state-of-the-art — by using geometric keypoint representations instead of RGB and an encoder-only design for computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: Automated sign language recognition for under-represented languages like CASL remains unsolved, with the CASL-W60 benchmark only reaching 69.93% accuracy. The common heuristic of fine-tuning high-resource models fails because of limited CASL data scale and a significant lexical/visual domain gap between CASL and large-scale corpora like WLASL, rendering pre-trained representations uninformative.
AI.method: TransSLR is a lightweight Temporal Transformer Encoder trained from scratch on 64-frame normalized pose sequences, using average pooling and a classification head. It operates on geometric keypoint representations rather than raw RGB, enabling signer-independent generalization without relying on visual appearance, and its encoder-only design reduces computational overhead.
AI.result: TransSLR achieves a new state-of-the-art accuracy of 80.39% on the CASL-W60 benchmark, surpassing the previous best by +10.46%. Extensive experiments comparing against RGB-based and multimodal baselines confirm state-of-the-art performance with significantly reduced computational cost.
AI.conclusion: TransSLR demonstrates that training from scratch on lightweight pose representations with an encoder-only transformer architecture can effectively overcome the data scarcity and domain gap challenges in under-resourced sign language recognition, making deployment feasible in resource-constrained environments.

title: Test-Time Adaptation with Online Personalized Energy-Based Cache for Fine-Grained Video Expression Recognition
summary: Facial expression recognition (FER) in videos is challenging because models must identify subtle, temporally evolving affective states that vary across individuals. Although vision-language models provide transferable visual-semantic representations, models trained on subject-independent data often degrade under subject-specific distribution shifts at inference time. Existing test-time adaptation (TTA) methods commonly update model parameters during inference, increasing computational cost and latency. Cache-based methods avoid parameter updates, but they usually require enough target samples to form reliable class prototypes, which is difficult early in adaptation and for rarely observed classes. We introduce Energy-Based Cache Personalization (EB-CaP), a subject-based online TTA method for video FER that generates class-specific prototypes personalized to each target video. EB-CaP uses a lightweight energy-based model to sample prototypes from the current unlabeled video and populate a personalized cache online, without accumulating large amounts of target data or storing diverse source prototypes. Its energy function relies only on pretrained CLIP: similarities between the target video embedding and class text embeddings guide prototype sampling. In parallel, positive and negative caches store reliable and uncertain target embeddings. An adaptive entropy gate controls cache updates according to the evolving confidence distribution, while a diversity gate limits redundant samples. Final predictions combine cache-derived scores with the current CLIP scores. Experiments on BioVid, StressID, and BAH show that EB-CaP outperforms state-of-the-art TTA methods while maintaining low computational and memory overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/MasoumehSharafi/EB-CaP.

AI.tldr: EB-CaP is a subject-based online test-time adaptation method for video facial expression recognition that uses a lightweight energy-based model to generate personalized class prototypes from unlabeled target videos, populating an online cache without accumulating target data or storing source prototypes, with adaptive entropy and diversity gates to control cache updates, outperforming SOTA TTA methods on BioVid, StressID, and BAH.
AI.motivation: Video FER models trained on subject-independent data degrade under subject-specific distribution shifts at inference time. Existing TTA methods either update parameters (costly, high latency) or use cache-based approaches that require many target samples to form reliable prototypes, which is difficult early in adaptation and for rare classes.
AI.method: EB-CaP leverages a lightweight energy-based model (based on CLIP similarities between target video and class text embeddings) to sample and generate personalized class prototypes from the current unlabeled video, populating a positive cache (reliable) and negative cache (uncertain) online. An adaptive entropy gate controls cache updates based on confidence distribution, and a diversity gate limits redundant samples. Final predictions combine cache-derived scores with current CLIP scores.
AI.result: EB-CaP outperforms state-of-the-art TTA methods on BioVid, StressID, and BAH benchmarks while maintaining low computational and memory overhead.
AI.conclusion: The proposed energy-based cache personalization provides an efficient, parameter-free online TTA approach for subject-specific video FER, avoiding both the computational cost of parameter updates and the data accumulation requirements of traditional cache methods.

title: InsertFuse: A Unified Framework for Multi-Category Reference-Guided Image Insertion
summary: We present InsertFuse, a unified framework for multi-category reference-guided image insertion. Its key idea is to decouple category-specific expertise learning from cross-category capability consolidation. InsertFuse first trains specialized experts for different insertion categories and then introduces Insertion On-Policy Distillation (IOPD) to consolidate their capabilities into a single student. By querying the matched expert at states visited by the student, IOPD preserves category-specific insertion behavior while mitigating the cross-category interference caused by direct joint training. To improve spatial control, we propose Token-Aligned Geometry Conditioning (TAGC), which maps mask-derived geometric cues to the visual token grid, and Region-Balanced Flow Matching, which separately normalizes prediction errors inside and outside the insertion region to prevent background-dominated and scale-dependent supervision. We further introduce Reference CFG to isolate and strengthen the guidance induced by the visual reference under fixed scene and geometry conditions, with IOPD transferring this enhanced supervision into the unified student. Extensive experiments on the public AnyInsertion benchmark and our multi-category test set demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on most metrics, showing strong reference fidelity and generation quality across diverse insertion categories.

AI.tldr: InsertFuse is a unified framework for multi-category reference-guided image insertion that decouples category-specific expert training from cross-category capability consolidation via Insertion On-Policy Distillation, enhanced by Token-Aligned Geometry Conditioning, Region-Balanced Flow Matching, and Reference CFG, achieving state-of-the-art performance on public benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Multi-category reference-guided image insertion is challenging because directly training a single model across different insertion categories causes cross-category interference. The authors aim to unify diverse insertion capabilities in one model while preserving category-specific behavior and improving spatial control.
AI.method: The framework decouples category-specific expertise learning from cross-category consolidation: (1) trains specialized experts per insertion category, (2) uses Insertion On-Policy Distillation (IOPD) to consolidate experts into a single student by querying matched experts at student-visited states, (3) Token-Aligned Geometry Conditioning (TAGC) maps mask-derived geometric cues to the visual token grid, (4) Region-Balanced Flow Matching normalizes prediction errors inside/outside insertion regions separately, and (5) Reference CFG isolates and strengthens visual reference guidance, with IOPD transferring this enhanced supervision into the unified student.
AI.result: Experiments on the public AnyInsertion benchmark and a multi-category test set demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on most metrics, showing strong reference fidelity and generation quality across diverse insertion categories.
AI.conclusion: The proposed decoupling strategy with expert distillation effectively mitigates cross-category interference, while the geometry conditioning, region-balanced supervision, and reference guidance enhancements collectively improve spatial control and reference fidelity, establishing a new state of the art for multi-category reference-guided image insertion.

title: Improving Low-Resolution Face Recognition under Limited Data: How Synthetic Data Generation Can Close the Domain Gap
comment: Accepted at IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB) 2026, Focus Session on Generative AI for Fair and Secure Biometrics under Limited Data
summary: Face Recognition (FR) systems in surveillance settings often encounter Low Resolution (LR) faces, those whose face region falls below the standard 112 $\times$ 112 input size. While labelled High Resolution (HR) training data is abundant, labelled native-LR data, and above all paired native LR/HR data, is scarce. One workaround is to synthesize LR data from the available HR faces, but how much synthesis effort is repaid in recognition accuracy remains unclear. We present a study of simple synthetic generation strategies for a compact, edge device-oriented face recognition system, spanning interpolation-based degradation, knowledge distillation, a Prepended Domain Transformer (PDT), Real ESRGAN-style degradation, and a learned Super Resolution (SR) front-end with an identity-aware loss. We evaluate these strategies on synthetic cross-resolution face benchmarks (LFW, CFP-FP, AgeDB-30) and on TinyFace, a real-world native LR dataset, and expose a synthetic-real gap: the degradation setting that is optimal on synthetic benchmarks is not the one that is optimal on real LR. We find that more synthesis effort does not help monotonically: the learned SR front-end does not surpass a direct feed of the aligned LR image into a strong backbone, while simple interpolation augmentation of a compact backbone is the only synthesis that improves over its own baseline. We conclude that generative methods for LR face recognition must be validated on real LR and against a direct-feed baseline, and release our pipeline at https://idiap.ch/paper/synth-lrfr

AI.tldr: A study of synthetic LR face generation strategies for compact, edge-device FR systems, finding that simple interpolation augmentation beats more complex generative approaches, and revealing a synthetic-real gap where optimal synthetic benchmarks do not transfer to real native-LR data.
AI.motivation: Labelled native-LR face data, especially paired LR/HR data, is scarce in surveillance FR settings, while HR training data is abundant. Synthesis from HR is a common workaround, but whether synthesis effort translates into recognition accuracy gains is unclear.
AI.method: Compares multiple synthetic degradation strategies—interpolation-based degradation, knowledge distillation, Prepended Domain Transformer (PDT), Real ESRGAN-style degradation, and a learned Super Resolution (SR) front-end with identity-aware loss—on a compact edge-device-oriented FR system, evaluated on synthetic cross-resolution benchmarks (LFW, CFP-FP, AgeDB-30) and real-world TinyFace.
AI.result: A synthetic-real gap exists: the optimal degradation on synthetic benchmarks is not optimal on real LR. More synthesis effort does not help monotonically—learned SR front-end fails to surpass direct LR feeding into a strong backbone, while simple interpolation augmentation of a compact backbone is the only synthesis improving over its baseline.
AI.conclusion: Generative methods for LR face recognition must be validated on real LR data and against a direct-feed baseline; simple synthetic strategies can be more effective than complex generative approaches.

title: Toward surface-based registration of a virtual preoperative cutting guide onto the mandible for reconstruction surgery
summary: Mandibular reconstruction restores facial continuity and oral function after segmental resection. Patient-specific cutting guides transfer a computed tomography (CT)-based plan to the operating room with three-dimensional information, but printed guides add cost and lead time, cannot adapt after fabrication, and may interrupt surgery if sterility is lost. We investigate a markerless augmented reality (AR) alternative that registers a virtual cutting guide to the exposed mandible from surface geometry. The method extends surface-based registration for the transoral setting, where teeth form the most distinctive visible surface. After camera calibration, a HoloLens 2 time-of-flight camera captures a partial intraoperative point cloud. The user supplies a rough head-based alignment only to crop the region of interest. A teeth-weighted global stage computes correspondences and solves a truncated least-squares rigid alignment. An asymmetric point-to-plane iterative closest point (ICP) stage refines the complete CT mandible against the partial depth cloud target. The guide-to-mandible transform places the guide in the HoloLens world frame, while pose updates and interpolation follow target motion. We define a blinded phantom protocol with 30 target registration error (TRE) points under full, intermediate, and teeth-only exposure, plus a motion-to-display latency test. Our median TRE is 4.05, 6.10, and 7.10 mm respectively, and median latency is 0.805 s. These values support the feasibility of using AR to replace physical prints. The workflow removes mounted fiducials and manual landmark selection and provides a testable path toward transoral cutting guidance.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a markerless augmented reality (AR) system for mandibular reconstruction that registers a virtual cutting guide to the exposed mandible using surface geometry captured by a HoloLens 2 time-of-flight camera, achieving median target registration errors of 4.05-7.10 mm across different exposure levels and 0.805 s latency, demonstrating feasibility as an alternative to physical printed guides.
AI.motivation: Patient-specific cutting guides for mandibular reconstruction are printed from CT-based plans, but physical prints add cost and lead time, cannot adapt after fabrication, and may interrupt surgery if sterility is compromised. An AR-based virtual alternative could overcome these limitations.
AI.method: The method uses a markerless AR approach with a HoloLens 2 time-of-flight camera to capture a partial intraoperative point cloud. After camera calibration, a rough head-based alignment crops the region of interest. A teeth-weighted global stage computes correspondences and solves truncated least-squares rigid alignment, followed by an asymmetric point-to-plane ICP stage refining the complete CT mandible against the partial depth cloud. The guide-to-mandible transform places the guide in the HoloLens world frame, with pose updates and interpolation following target motion.
AI.result: In a blinded phantom protocol with 30 TRE points under full, intermediate, and teeth-only exposure, median TRE was 4.05, 6.10, and 7.10 mm respectively, with a median motion-to-display latency of 0.805 s.
AI.conclusion: The achieved accuracy and latency support the feasibility of using AR to replace physical printed cutting guides for mandibular reconstruction, removing the need for mounted fiducials and manual landmark selection while providing a testable path toward transoral cutting guidance.

title: SLED: Scalable Location Encoding via Distillation
summary: The plethora of readily available geospatial data offers exciting opportunities to learn high quality representations of the planet, but the sheer size of the Earth Observations (EO), differing modalities, and different sensor types pose significant challenges in doing so. Location encoders have emerged as an efficient way of compressing EOs into location-specific embeddings. However, current state-of-the-art location encoders rely on computationally expensive CLIP-style frameworks that require large batch sizes in the 16K--32K range, suffer from false negative samples, and scale poorly with additional modalities. We introduce the Scalable Location Encoder via Distillation (SLED), a distillation-based location encoder that uses geospatial location as a binding modality to pretrain location encoders with any modality of geospatial data. The resulting location encoder framework is lightweight, modular, and can flexibly incorporate multiple modes, while eliminating the need for spatiotemporal coregistration of samples. SLED is performant with batch sizes as small as 128, enabling pretraining at a fraction of the runtime and compute costs of current state-of-the-art models. We demonstrate our approach by pretraining unimodal and multimodal SLED models on Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat imagery. We show that both unimodal and multimodal SLED models keep pace with or outperform existing approaches on a diverse set of 19 human-centric benchmark tasks and explore the benefits of using additional modes in pretraining.

AI.tldr: SLED introduces a distillation-based location encoder that uses geospatial location as a binding modality to pretrain location encoders with any modality of geospatial data, achieving state-of-the-art performance with batch sizes as small as 128 instead of the 16K-32K required by CLIP-style frameworks, while significantly reducing runtime and compute costs.
AI.motivation: Current state-of-the-art location encoders rely on computationally expensive CLIP-style frameworks that require large batch sizes (16K-32K), suffer from false negative samples, and scale poorly with additional modalities, making them inefficient for learning representations from the vast and diverse Earth Observation data.
AI.method: SLED uses a distillation-based approach with geospatial location as a binding modality to pretrain location encoders with any modality of geospatial data. The framework is lightweight and modular, eliminating the need for spatiotemporal coregistration of samples while flexibly incorporating multiple modalities.
AI.result: SLED performs well with batch sizes as small as 128, reducing runtime and compute costs. Unimodal and multimodal SLED models pretrained on Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, and Landsat imagery keep pace with or outperform existing approaches on 19 diverse human-centric benchmark tasks.
AI.conclusion: Distillation-based location encoding with location as a binding modality offers a scalable, efficient, and flexible alternative to CLIP-style pretraining, achieving competitive performance at a fraction of the computational cost while supporting multiple modalities.

title: Do 3D Medical Foundation Models See Through MRI Artifacts? A Controlled Study of Representation Robustness
comment: Accepted at the ECCV 2026 Workshop on Artificial Intelligence for Medical 3D Vision (AI4M3D)
summary: Self-supervised 3D medical foundation models are increasingly used as general-purpose feature extractors, yet their sensitivity to MRI artifacts remains poorly understood. We present a controlled evaluation of representation robustness across five pretrained 3D encoders spanning different architectures, objectives, pretraining domains, and dataset scales. Using BraTS-Africa cases with four MRI sequences, we generate seven frequency- and image-domain artifacts at five predefined corruption settings. Robustness is assessed using linear centered kernel alignment (CKA), RankMe, and UMAP, complemented by an independent segmentation-consistency analysis. We find that robustness is strongly model- and artifact-dependent. 3DINO exhibits the most consistently stable representations, while BrainIAC is highly sensitive to several corruptions; NeuroVFM, BrainFM, and Neuro-SimCLR show intermediate but distinct artifact-specific profiles. Across many conditions, CKA decreases substantially while RankMe remains comparatively stable, indicating that artifacts often distort representation geometry without causing dimensional collapse. Segmentation consistency also degrades under corruption, particularly for ghosting and Rician noise, but aligns only partially with representation-level robustness. These findings show that larger-scale or domain-specific pretraining alone does not guarantee artifact invariance and motivate explicit robustness evaluation before deploying 3D foundation models in heterogeneous MRI settings.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically evaluates the robustness of five pretrained 3D self-supervised medical foundation models against MRI artifacts, finding that representation robustness is highly model- and artifact-dependent, with 3DINO being most stable, BrainIAC most sensitive, and larger-scale or domain-specific pretraining not guaranteeing artifact invariance.
AI.motivation: Self-supervised 3D medical foundation models are widely used as general-purpose feature extractors, but their sensitivity to MRI artifacts remains poorly understood, necessitating a controlled evaluation of representation robustness.
AI.method: Using BraTS-Africa cases with four MRI sequences, seven frequency- and image-domain artifacts are generated at five corruption settings. Robustness is assessed via linear centered kernel alignment (CKA), RankMe, and UMAP, complemented by an independent segmentation-consistency analysis across five pretrained 3D encoders with different architectures, objectives, pretraining domains, and dataset scales.
AI.result: Robustness is strongly model- and artifact-dependent. 3DINO shows the most stable representations while BrainIAC is highly sensitive; NeuroVFM, BrainFM, and Neuro-SimCLR are intermediate with distinct artifact-specific profiles. CKA decreases substantially under corruption while RankMe remains stable, indicating distorted geometry without dimensional collapse. Segmentation consistency degrades under ghosting and Rician noise but only partially aligns with representation-level robustness.
AI.conclusion: Larger-scale or domain-specific pretraining does not guarantee artifact invariance, motivating explicit robustness evaluation before deploying 3D foundation models in heterogeneous real-world MRI settings.

title: When Semantics Saturate or Emerge: Adaptation-Conditional Semantic Utility in Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
summary: Language descriptions in source-free cross-domain few-shot learning (SF-CDFSL) are often selected according to zero-shot accuracy obtained with a frozen vision--language model. This paper asks whether that ranking remains valid after target-domain visual adaptation. Under a strictly paired protocol, we compare a generic class-name template with fixed detailed class descriptions before and after visual Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on EuroSAT, CropDisease, ISIC, and ChestX. Let $\deltazero$ and $\deltalora$ denote the Detailed-minus-Base accuracy before and after adaptation, respectively. Two recurring regimes emerge. In \emph{semantic saturation}, $\deltazero>0$ but $0<\deltalora\ll\deltazero$: on EuroSAT and CropDisease, initial gains of 8.13--21.54 percentage points contract to 0.69--2.96 points after LoRA. In \emph{semantic emergence}, $\deltazero\leq0$ but $\deltalora>0$: on ISIC and ChestX, detailed descriptions become more useful only after the visual representation is updated. Training trajectories and sample-level decomposition show that saturation is driven mainly by Base-LoRA recovering errors already solved by detailed semantics, whereas emergence is associated with prediction turnover and newly formed Detailed-only correct decisions. Fixed-point-free shuffled-semantic controls, a second CLIP backbone, and multiple random seeds support the broad pattern while identifying ChestX 1-shot as a weak boundary case. These findings establish that zero-shot prompt quality is an incomplete proxy for adaptation-anchor quality and motivate evaluating language on both sides of the adaptation boundary.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates whether zero-shot accuracy ranking of language descriptions in source-free cross-domain few-shot learning (SF-CDFSL) remains valid after target-domain visual adaptation via LoRA. Using a strictly paired protocol comparing generic class-name templates with detailed descriptions across four datasets, the authors identify two regimes: semantic saturation (where initial detailed-description gains vanish after adaptation) and semantic emergence (where detailed descriptions only become useful after visual updates). They conclude that zero-shot prompt quality is an incomplete proxy for adaptation-anchor quality.
AI.motivation: Language descriptions in SF-CDFSL are typically selected based on zero-shot accuracy using a frozen vision-language model, but it is unclear whether this ranking remains valid after target-domain visual adaptation. The authors aim to test this assumption empirically.
AI.method: The authors use a strictly paired protocol comparing generic class-name templates with fixed detailed class descriptions before and after visual Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on four datasets (EuroSAT, CropDisease, ISIC, ChestX). They compute Detailed-minus-Base accuracy before (δ_zero) and after (δ_lora) adaptation, analyze training trajectories and sample-level decomposition, and validate with shuffled-semantic controls, a second CLIP backbone, and multiple random seeds.
AI.result: Two regimes emerge: (1) Semantic saturation on EuroSAT and CropDisease where initial gains (8.13-21.54 points) contract dramatically (0.69-2.96 points) after LoRA; (2) Semantic emergence on ISIC and ChestX where detailed descriptions only become useful after visual adaptation. Saturation is driven by Base-LoRA recovering errors solved by detailed semantics, while emergence involves prediction turnover and newly formed Detailed-only correct decisions. ChestX 1-shot is identified as a weak boundary case.
AI.conclusion: Zero-shot prompt quality is an incomplete proxy for adaptation-anchor quality. The paper motivates evaluating language descriptions on both sides of the adaptation boundary, rather than relying solely on frozen zero-shot performance for description selection in SF-CDFSL.

title: Corrupting Attention: Evasion-Based Adversarial Attacks on Encoder Attention in Detection Transformers
summary: Adversarial vulnerabilities remain a major concern for the safe deployment of neural networks, particularly in object detection, a core task embedded in many safety-critical systems. Detection transformers have emerged as leading object detectors, yet their adversarial robustness remains comparatively underexplored. Most existing attacks target the detection output rather than the attention mechanism that makes these models distinctive. In this paper, we introduce the first attack that directly optimizes an encoder-attention objective under an imperceptible, bounded $\ell_\infty$ perturbation. Rather than introducing an attacker-owned sink token through a visible patch, it drives the model's own attention toward a corrupted target. We argue that encoder attention concentrates the model's spatial reasoning, so corrupting it propagates through the detection pipeline more disruptively than perturbing the detection output alone. Our attack reduces DETR-R50 mAP on COCO from 42.1 to 0.97, a $\sim 4\times$ reduction in resulting mAP over the strongest existing attack under an identical perturbation budget and iteration count. We further show that this vulnerability is not specific to a particular corruption objective: across four qualitatively distinct targets, dispersion, re-ranking, permutation, and peak-suppression, detection consistently drops below 3 mAP, suggesting that the weakness arises from disrupting the attention structure itself rather than from any single target. Finally, we demonstrate that the attack generalizes across attention formulations, reducing DINO-Swin-L from 56.8 to 1.44 mAP against 7.3 for the strongest prior attack, establishing state-of-the-art on both dense and deformable attention.

AI.tldr: Introduces the first attack on detection transformers that directly optimizes an encoder-attention objective under imperceptible bounded ℓ∞ perturbation, reducing DETR-R50 mAP from 42.1 to 0.97 (4× better than strongest prior attack) and generalizing across attention formulations including DINO-Swin-L.
AI.motivation: Detection transformers are leading object detectors but their adversarial robustness is underexplored. Existing attacks target detection output rather than the attention mechanism that distinguishes these models. Encoder attention concentrates spatial reasoning, so corrupting it should be more disruptive than perturbing detection output alone.
AI.method: The attack directly optimizes an encoder-attention objective under imperceptible, bounded ℓ∞ perturbation. Instead of introducing an attacker-owned sink token via a visible patch, it drives the model's own attention toward a corrupted target. The authors evaluate four distinct corruption targets (dispersion, re-ranking, permutation, peak-suppression) and test across different attention formulations.
AI.result: Reduces DETR-R50 mAP on COCO from 42.1 to 0.97, a ~4× reduction in resulting mAP over the strongest existing attack under identical perturbation budget and iteration count. All four corruption targets drop detection below 3 mAP. Attack generalizes across attention formulations, reducing DINO-Swin-L from 56.8 to 1.44 mAP versus 7.3 for the strongest prior attack.
AI.conclusion: The vulnerability in detection transformers stems from disrupting the attention structure itself rather than any single corruption target. This establishes state-of-the-art adversarial attacks on both dense and deformable attention in detection transformers, highlighting attention as a critical weak point for robust deployment.

title: CoDAT: Collaborative Dual-Attention Transformer with Low-Cost Temporal Modeling for Efficient Edge Action Recognition
summary: Real-time human action recognition on Internet-of-Things (IoT) edge devices requires models that capture rich spatio-temporal cues within strict latency, memory, and power envelopes. Current 3D CNNs, video transformers, and shift-based ViT deliver high accuracy but come at computational costs that preclude edge IoT deployment. This paper proposes CoDAT, a Collaborative Dual-Attention Transformer that replaces conventional multi-head attention with a lightweight dual-branch module: Spatial Convolutional Attention (SCA) for local aggregation and Strided Single-Head Attention (SSHA) for global context. SSHA jointly compresses the spatial resolution and channel dimensions of the query, key, and value tensors via stride-based sparse projection, then fuses the resulting global and local features at a markedly reduced cost. To enable temporal communication across frames, a parameter-free TShift module is embedded in each block. Extensive experiments on Jetson AGX Orin and Raspberry Pi 5 demonstrate that CoDAT achieves an energy-accuracy balance in both image and action recognition. On ImageNet-1K, CoDAT-M runs 2x faster than EfficientViT384 and FastViT-S12 at comparable accuracy, and CoDAT-L matches ViT-S with 3x fewer parameters at 2x higher throughput. On Kinetics-400 and MA-52, CoDAT achieves competitive Top-1 accuracy against state-of-the-art CNN, transformer, and hybrid baselines while running up to 2.9x faster than VSwin-T, 2x faster than ViT-Temporal-Shift variants, and 5x faster than UniFormer-B. On UCF-101, CoDAT-S384 matches TokShift and LAPS while being 6x faster and requiring up to 13x fewer FLOPs, establishing an efficiency-accuracy balance for real-time action recognition in edge IoT perception systems. Code is available at https://github.com/novendrastywn/CoDAT .

AI.tldr: CoDAT is a Collaborative Dual-Attention Transformer for real-time action recognition on IoT edge devices, using Spatial Convolutional Attention (SCA) for local aggregation and Strided Single-Head Attention (SSHA) for global context, achieving superior speed and energy efficiency on Jetson AGX Orin and Raspberry Pi 5 while maintaining competitive accuracy on ImageNet-1K, Kinetics-400, and other benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Real-time human action recognition on IoT edge devices demands models capturing rich spatio-temporal cues within strict latency, memory, and power constraints. Existing 3D CNNs, video transformers, and shift-based ViTs achieve high accuracy but at computational costs that preclude edge deployment.
AI.method: CoDAT replaces conventional multi-head attention with a lightweight dual-branch module: SCA for local aggregation and SSHA for global context. SSHA jointly compresses spatial resolution and channel dimensions of Q, K, V tensors via stride-based sparse projection and fuses global/local features at reduced cost. A parameter-free TShift module enables temporal communication across frames.
AI.result: On ImageNet-1K, CoDAT-M runs 2x faster than EfficientViT384 and FastViT-S12 at comparable accuracy; CoDAT-L matches ViT-S with 3x fewer parameters at 2x higher throughput. On Kinetics-400/MA-52, it achieves competitive Top-1 accuracy while running up to 2.9x faster than VSwin-T, 2x faster than ViT-Temporal-Shift variants, and 5x faster than UniFormer-B. On UCF-101, CoDAT-S384 matches TokShift and LAPS while being 6x faster with up to 13x fewer FLOPs.
AI.conclusion: CoDAT establishes an efficiency-accuracy balance for real-time action recognition in edge IoT perception systems, demonstrating strong potential for deployment on resource-constrained devices.

title: Suppress and Diversify: Refining Robust Pathways for Corruption Robustness
summary: Model robustness against natural image corruptions is essential for safety-critical applications. While existing methods primarily focus on implicit representation learning, we provide the first systematic exploration of computational pathways to explicitly characterize internal robustness. We identify a progressive decay of robust features across network layers and establish a functional dependency between the prevalence of these features and model performance. To exploit these insights, we propose Suppress and Diversify (S\&D), a non-intrusive refinement approach that enhances robustness by dynamically selecting robust pathways and diversifying them through symmetry-preserving transformations. S\&D is architecture-agnostic, parameter-free, and incurs zero test-time overhead. Extensive evaluations across eight benchmarks demonstrate that S\&D consistently improves performance across multiple vision tasks, diverse backbones, and complex real-world scenarios, highlighting its broad efficacy and scalability.

AI.tldr: This paper provides the first systematic exploration of computational pathways to explicitly characterize internal robustness against natural image corruptions. It identifies a progressive decay of robust features across network layers and proposes Suppress and Diversify (S&D), a non-intrusive, architecture-agnostic, parameter-free refinement approach that dynamically selects and diversifies robust pathways via symmetry-preserving transformations, achieving consistent performance gains across eight benchmarks with zero test-time overhead.
AI.motivation: Model robustness against natural image corruptions is essential for safety-critical applications. Existing methods primarily focus on implicit representation learning, and there is a lack of explicit, systematic understanding of how robustness is internally characterized within network architectures.
AI.method: The paper identifies a progressive decay of robust features across network layers and establishes a functional dependency between feature prevalence and model performance. Based on these insights, they propose Suppress and Diversify (S&D), a non-intrusive refinement approach that dynamically selects robust pathways and diversifies them through symmetry-preserving transformations. The method is architecture-agnostic, parameter-free, and adds zero test-time overhead.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations across eight benchmarks demonstrate that S&D consistently improves performance across multiple vision tasks, diverse backbones, and complex real-world scenarios, highlighting its broad efficacy and scalability.
AI.conclusion: The proposed S&D approach provides a novel, explicit computational pathway perspective on internal robustness, achieving consistent robustness improvements across diverse settings without requiring architectural modifications, extra parameters, or test-time costs.

title: WaveFreqAnchor: Wave-Structural Anchoring and Frequency Correction Diffusion for Training-Free Face Restoration
comment: training-free wavelet-structural diffusion sampling framework for face restoration that improves structural stability, identity consistency, and real-world perceptual quality without task-specific fine-tuning
summary: Diffusion-based face restoration that adjusts the sampling trajectory of pre-trained diffusion models has achieved remarkable progress. However, existing approaches provide insufficient constraints during reverse diffusion, causing identity-related structural drift and degraded fidelity under severe degradations. To address this, we propose WaveFreqAnchor, a training-free framework based on Wave-Structural Anchoring and Frequency Correction Diffusion. Specifically, Anchor-Space Wave-Structural Guidance (ASWG) constrains facial structures through anisotropic wave-response consistency, while Multi-scale Wavelet-Fourier Injection (MWFI) aligns the predicted low-frequency subband with the observation by replacing its phase, correcting inconsistencies accumulated during reverse diffusion. For real-world scenes, we further introduce Subband High-Frequency Enhancement (SHE), which performs bounded, spatially masked refinement on the predicted high-frequency subbands to recover fine facial details under unknown compound degradations. Together, these designs effectively preserve facial identity while restoring sharp and realistic facial details. Extensive experiments show that our method consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving high-quality and high-fidelity face restoration.

AI.tldr: WaveFreqAnchor is a training-free diffusion-based face restoration framework combining Wave-Structural Anchoring and Frequency Correction Diffusion to preserve facial identity and restore sharp details under severe degradations.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based face restoration approaches provide insufficient constraints during reverse diffusion, causing identity-related structural drift and degraded fidelity under severe degradations.
AI.method: Three components: (1) Anchor-Space Wave-Structural Guidance (ASWG) constrains facial structures via anisotropic wave-response consistency; (2) Multi-scale Wavelet-Fourier Injection (MWFI) aligns predicted low-frequency subbands with observations by phase replacement; (3) Subband High-Frequency Enhancement (SHE) performs bounded, spatially masked refinement on high-frequency subbands for real-world compound degradations.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent superiority over existing methods in achieving high-quality and high-fidelity face restoration.
AI.conclusion: WaveFreqAnchor effectively preserves facial identity while restoring sharp and realistic facial details through combined wave-structural and frequency-domain constraints.

title: Beyond Starry Night: Shortcut-Aware Control-State Planning for Artist-Grounded Text to Image Generation
comment: 47 pages, 13 figures, including appendices. Kuan Xing and Ye Wang contributed equally
summary: Artist-grounded image generation requires more than appending an artist name to a prompt. Image models often respond to artist names through canonical shortcuts, such as recurring motifs, generic palettes, or overrepresented period signatures, rather than preserving the user's intended scene. We introduce Atelier, a shortcut-aware control-state planning framework for artist-grounded image generation. Atelier translates underspecified artistic intent into an explicit control state that separates scene anchors, preserve/transform decisions, style-regime hypotheses, role-bound artist evidence, and shortcut-avoidance constraints. It grounds this state using artist-level knowledge and local patch references, compiles backend-aware generation plans, and iteratively refines candidates through global and local authenticity feedback. We further introduce ArtIntentBench, a benchmark covering Van Gogh and Qi Baishi across artwork re-rendering, period/style-controlled generation, historically unseen subjects, shortcut auditing, and human preference evaluation. Across open-weight and closed-source generators, Atelier improves artist-level style fidelity, preserves source structure more faithfully, and substantially reduces shortcut substitution compared with prompt-engineered, retrieval-augmented, and general-purpose agent baselines. These results suggest that artist-grounded generation is bottlenecked not only by image synthesis, but by the upstream inference of explicit, evidence-grounded artistic controls.

AI.tldr: Atelier is a shortcut-aware control-state planning framework for artist-grounded image generation that separates scene anchors, preserve/transform decisions, style hypotheses, and shortcut-avoidance constraints, outperforming baselines in style fidelity and shortcut reduction on the new ArtIntentBench benchmark.
AI.motivation: Artist-grounded image generation fails because models respond to artist names through canonical shortcuts (recurring motifs, generic palettes) rather than preserving the user's intended scene. The authors argue the bottleneck is not image synthesis but the inference of explicit, evidence-grounded artistic controls.
AI.method: Atelier translates underspecified artistic intent into an explicit control state (scene anchors, preserve/transform decisions, style-regime hypotheses, role-bound artist evidence, shortcut-avoidance constraints), grounds it with artist-level knowledge and local patch references, compiles backend-aware generation plans, and iteratively refines candidates via global and local authenticity feedback. Introduces ArtIntentBench covering Van Gogh and Qi Baishi.
AI.result: Across open-weight and closed-source generators, Atelier improves artist-level style fidelity, preserves source structure more faithfully, and substantially reduces shortcut substitution compared with prompt-engineered, retrieval-augmented, and general-purpose agent baselines.
AI.conclusion: Artist-grounded generation is bottlenecked by upstream inference of explicit, evidence-grounded artistic controls rather than image synthesis alone, suggesting the need for planning-based control-state approaches.

title: Explore or Converge? Stage-Guided Per-Step Optimization for Diffusion Models
summary:
Diffusion models have strong generative capabilities. However, their maximum likelihood training objective only focuses on reconstructing the data distribution, making it difficult to align with specific preferences. Reinforcement learning (RL) for preference alignment in diffusion models is promising but limited by reward sparsity. Since a single reward cannot support optimization, existing RL methods usually backpropagate the final reward to all previous steps. However, denoising is stage-wise, with distinct semantics and controllability. Repeating the final reward across all steps creates a temporal objective mismatch, encouraging reward shortcuts that lead to reward hacking. At the same time, due to reward backfilling, each time step receives the same reward, making it impossible to distinguish between actions, thereby weakening the optimization process.
  To resolve this issue, we propose Stage-Guided Per-Step Optimization (SGPO) for diffusion models, which jointly leverages signal-to-noise ratio and semantic changes to identify generation stages and adaptively assign stage-specific objectives. Early denoising is chaotic and far from the final reward, resulting in weak reward-behavior correlation. This stage should prioritize exiting the chaotic state. In the mid stage, the latent transitions to a stable structure, where the final reward better corresponds to generative behavior. Therefore, this stage optimizes the final reward while exploring diversity to avoid early convergence to a single mode.
  In the late stage, the latent's core structure is largely fixed, and preference optimization mainly amplifies local details, risking overfitting. Therefore, stable convergence is preferred to avoid quality degradation. Results from 16 comparative experiments validate SGPO. Our method achieves 26.7% average gains in generative quality and 36.7% higher convergence speed.

AI.tldr: SGPO is a stage-guided per-step optimization framework for aligning diffusion models with preferences via RL, which identifies generation stages using signal-to-noise ratio and semantic changes, then assigns stage-specific objectives (exit chaos early, optimize final reward with diversity mid, and stable convergence late) to avoid reward hacking and temporal objective mismatch.
AI.motivation: Diffusion models trained with maximum likelihood struggle to align with specific user preferences. While RL for preference alignment is promising, existing methods backpropagate a single sparse final reward to all denoising steps, creating a temporal objective mismatch that encourages reward shortcuts and reward hacking. Moreover, identical rewards across all steps make it impossible to distinguish between actions, weakening the optimization signal.
AI.method: SGPO identifies generation stages by jointly leveraging signal-to-noise ratio and semantic changes, then assigns stage-specific objectives: (1) early stage focuses on escaping chaotic states due to weak reward-behavior correlation; (2) mid stage optimizes the final reward while encouraging diversity to prevent premature mode collapse; (3) late stage prioritizes stable convergence to avoid overfitting and quality degradation when core structure is already fixed.
AI.result: Across 16 comparative experiments, SGPO achieves 26.7% average gains in generative quality and 36.7% higher convergence speed compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: Stage-aware reward assignment resolves the temporal objective mismatch in diffusion model RL alignment, leading to better generative quality and faster convergence by respecting the distinct semantics and controllability of each denoising stage.

title: GraphVerse: A Comprehensive Visual Graph Reasoning Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Recent Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across diverse vision-language tasks, creating an urgent need for more challenging benchmarks. Yet existing evaluations still provide limited insight into whether these models can truly reason over structured visual information. Visual Graph Reasoning (VGR) offers a compelling testbed for this challenge, requiring models to integrate perception, structural understanding, and multi-step reasoning over graph-based visual inputs. However, prior VGR benchmarks often reduce the task to visual perception followed by text-based reasoning, restrict evaluation to single-image settings, rely on answer-only metrics, and underrepresent realistic graph-centric scenarios. To bridge the gap, we introduce GraphVerse, a unified benchmark that jointly evaluates perception, visual reasoning, and text-based graph reasoning in MLLMs under both single-image and paired-image settings. At its core is a suite of Graph-centric Image Editing (GIE) strategies that modify graph images while preserving their semantics, turning them into active tests of visual reasoning. We further propose VGR-Score, a process-sensitive metric that evaluates reasoning quality beyond final-answer accuracy. Extensive experiments reveal several key limitations of current MLLMs in VGR, while also validating the effectiveness of GIE strategies and the transferability of GraphVerse to broader multimodal reasoning capabilities. The code is available at https://github.com/sunyuanfu/GraphVerse.

AI.tldr: GraphVerse is a unified benchmark for Visual Graph Reasoning (VGR) that jointly evaluates perception, visual reasoning, and text-based graph reasoning in MLLMs under both single-image and paired-image settings, using Graph-centric Image Editing (GIE) strategies and a process-sensitive VGR-Score metric.
AI.motivation: Existing VGR benchmarks reduce tasks to visual perception followed by text-based reasoning, restrict evaluation to single-image settings, rely solely on answer-only metrics, and underrepresent realistic graph-centric scenarios, thus failing to test whether MLLMs can truly reason over structured visual information.
AI.method: Introduces GraphVerse, a unified benchmark featuring Graph-centric Image Editing (GIE) strategies that modify graph images while preserving semantics to actively test visual reasoning, and proposes VGR-Score, a process-sensitive metric that evaluates reasoning quality beyond final-answer accuracy, covering both single-image and paired-image settings.
AI.result: Extensive experiments reveal key limitations of current MLLMs in VGR, validate the effectiveness of GIE strategies, and demonstrate the transferability of GraphVerse to broader multimodal reasoning capabilities.
AI.conclusion: GraphVerse provides a more comprehensive and challenging evaluation framework for VGR, exposing gaps in current MLLM reasoning abilities over structured visual information while offering a transferable benchmark for broader multimodal reasoning research.

title: AnyTrack: Unifying Visual Object Tracking with Any Modalities
comment: Accepted by ACM MM2026. More modifications may be performed
summary: Visual object tracking aims to continuously locate specific targets within sequential frames, evolving from single-modal methods to multi-modal ones. However, existing multi-modal trackers are typically designed for fixed modality combinations, requiring separate models for different inputs. This leads to a poor adaptability to missing or imperfect modalities, and limited generalization. To address these issues, we propose a novel unified framework called AnyTrack for object tracking with any modalities. Specifically, we design a Modality-aware Interaction Module (MIM) to facilitate dynamic interaction across diverse modalities. This module bridges modality discrepancies and aggregates temporal cues to maintain spatio-temporal consistency during cross-modal interaction. Furthermore, we introduce a Context Understanding Module (CUM) to establish spatial correspondence between visual features and target locations via global-local prompts. This module employs target-aware context modeling to enhance foreground-background discrimination for precise localization. Finally, to support the training and evaluation under diverse modalities, we extend existing multi-modal object tracking benchmarks by incorporating grayscale images, language descriptions, and audio clips. Extensive experiments with both complete and missing modality settings demonstrate that our AnyTrack achieves state-of-the-art performance, validating its effectiveness and flexibility. The source code is available at https://github.com/IdolLab/AnyTrack.

AI.tldr: AnyTrack is a unified framework for visual object tracking that handles any combination of modalities (RGB, grayscale, depth, language, audio) within a single model, featuring a Modality-aware Interaction Module (MIM) for cross-modal dynamic interaction and a Context Understanding Module (CUM) for target-aware spatial correspondence. It extends existing multi-modal benchmarks with additional modalities and achieves state-of-the-art performance under both complete and missing modality settings.
AI.motivation: Existing multi-modal trackers are designed for fixed modality combinations, requiring separate models for different inputs, which leads to poor adaptability to missing/imperfect modalities and limited generalization across diverse modality settings.
AI.method: Proposes a unified framework (AnyTrack) with two key modules: (1) Modality-aware Interaction Module (MIM) that enables dynamic cross-modal interaction, bridges modality discrepancies, and maintains spatio-temporal consistency via temporal cues; (2) Context Understanding Module (CUM) that establishes spatial correspondence between visual features and target locations through global-local prompts, using target-aware context modeling to enhance foreground-background discrimination. Additionally, existing benchmarks are extended with grayscale images, language descriptions, and audio clips.
AI.result: Extensive experiments with both complete and missing modality settings demonstrate that AnyTrack achieves state-of-the-art performance, validating its effectiveness and flexibility.
AI.conclusion: AnyTrack provides a flexible, unified solution for multi-modal object tracking that can handle arbitrary modality combinations, addressing the limitations of fixed-modality models and improving adaptability to missing or imperfect modalities.

title: UniCycleFlow: Bidirectional Unpaired Image Translation with a Shared Rectified Flow
summary: Bidirectional unpaired image translation must preserve source-specific structure while learning coherent transformations in both directions without paired supervision. Existing methods typically employ two direction-specific generators or train separate one-way models. Even when linked by cycle consistency, such models constrain only the round-trip endpoint reconstruction, without requiring the two directions to obey a common local transformation rule. We propose UniCycleFlow, a rectified-flow framework that represents bidirectional translation as forward and reverse integration of a single time-conditioned velocity field. This formulation organizes both directions within the same continuous dynamics, rather than coupling otherwise separate endpoint mappings. A key challenge is that unpaired data provide no meaningful source--target coupling from which rectified-flow trajectories can be constructed. UniCycleFlow addresses this challenge by learning deterministic source-conditioned endpoints whose marginal distributions are adversarially matched to the opposite domains. The resulting paths are regularized by stop-gradient self-flow matching for intermediate velocity supervision, discrete cycle closure for forward--reverse consistency, and representation path-velocity regularization for controlling localized feature changes along the trajectory. Across ten translation directions, UniCycleFlow achieves the lowest FID on 7 of 10 tasks using a single Euler evaluation and obtains the best average FID of 55.1.

AI.tldr: UniCycleFlow is a rectified-flow framework for bidirectional unpaired image translation that represents both translation directions as forward and reverse integration of a single time-conditioned velocity field, achieving the lowest FID on 7 of 10 tasks with a best average FID of 55.1.
AI.motivation: Existing bidirectional unpaired image translation methods use two separate generators or one-way models linked only by cycle consistency, which constrains round-trip endpoint reconstruction but fails to enforce a common local transformation rule between the two directions.
AI.method: UniCycleFlow formulates bidirectional translation as forward and reverse integration of a single time-conditioned velocity field. It learns deterministic source-conditioned endpoints whose marginal distributions are adversarially matched to the opposite domains, and regularizes the paths via stop-gradient self-flow matching, discrete cycle closure, and representation path-velocity regularization.
AI.result: Across ten translation directions, UniCycleFlow achieves the lowest FID on 7 of 10 tasks using a single Euler evaluation and obtains the best average FID of 55.1.
AI.conclusion: By unifying both translation directions within a single continuous dynamics framework and addressing the lack of source-target coupling in unpaired data through adversarial marginal matching, UniCycleFlow sets a new state-of-the-art for bidirectional unpaired image translation.

title: PAST: Prompt-Adaptive Sampling Termination for Efficient Diffusion Model
summary: While diffusion models have made significant progress in text-to-image tasks, they still exhibit limitations when directly optimizing downstream objectives. Although Reinforcement Learning (RL) enables targeted optimization, existing methods are generally constrained by low-efficiency fine-tuning and sparse rewards. To address these challenges, we propose PAST, which provides differentiated rewards while adaptively regulating training episode length by jointly perceiving denoising progress and prompt difficulty. Specifically, we design an intrinsic reward paradigm to compensate for sparse extrinsic rewards and guide the model to explore paths that diverge more efficiently from noise patterns. We further provide theoretical justification for intrinsic rewards. Then, PAST dynamically monitors denoising completion and semantic alignment between image structures and prompt semantics. When both metrics satisfy generation requirements, the system adaptively terminates training. This enables appropriate allocation of episode lengths based on prompt difficulty and the current generation process. Finally, based on the predicted residual noise level, we establish a dual adaptive coordination mechanism. Specifically, it not only balances the extrinsic and intrinsic rewards but also balances the exploration and convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that PAST enhances computational efficiency of existing RL fine-tuning methods by up to 66.7%, while improving preference optimization quality by up to 29.5% through its dual adaptive regulation mechanism.

AI.tldr: PAST is an RL fine-tuning framework for text-to-image diffusion models that provides differentiated intrinsic rewards and adaptively regulates training episode length by jointly perceiving denoising progress and prompt difficulty, improving computational efficiency by up to 66.7% and preference optimization quality by up to 29.5%.
AI.motivation: Diffusion models excel at text-to-image generation but struggle to directly optimize downstream objectives. While RL enables targeted optimization, existing methods suffer from low-efficiency fine-tuning and sparse rewards.
AI.method: PAST introduces: (1) an intrinsic reward paradigm with theoretical justification to compensate for sparse extrinsic rewards and guide more efficient exploration away from noise patterns; (2) adaptive training episode termination based on joint monitoring of denoising completion and semantic alignment between image structures and prompt semantics; (3) a dual adaptive coordination mechanism that balances extrinsic/intrinsic rewards and exploration/convergence based on predicted residual noise level.
AI.result: PAST enhances computational efficiency of existing RL fine-tuning methods by up to 66.7% and improves preference optimization quality by up to 29.5% through its dual adaptive regulation mechanism.
AI.conclusion: The proposed dual adaptive regulation mechanism—combining intrinsic rewards with adaptive episode length control—effectively addresses the low-efficiency fine-tuning and sparse reward challenges in RL-based diffusion model optimization.

title: AdvTiles: Physical Adversarial Camouflage Clothing against Person Detectors via Learnable Tiles
summary: Physical adversarial attacks against person detectors have evolved from localized patches to full-body textures. However, achieving both visual naturalness and strong attack effectiveness remains challenging. Existing natural-looking methods typically optimize camouflage textures as a whole, limiting the flexibility to refine local adversarial patterns and their spatial arrangement. To address this issue, we propose AdvTiles, a physical adversarial camouflage framework built from learnable tiles, enabling strong attack performance while preserving a natural camouflage appearance. Specifically, we use a Straight-through (ST) Gumbel-Softmax estimator for differentiable tile selection, enabling joint optimization of tile patterns and spatial layouts. This design provides fine-grained control over adversarial texture generation. To improve robustness in diverse physical conditions, we further optimize the camouflage through differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering with variations in viewpoints, scales, illuminations and backgrounds. Extensive experiments across multiple detectors demonstrate that AdvTiles achieves an average ASR of 86.2%, outperforming existing state-of-the-art attack methods. We further fabricate the optimized camouflage into wearable adversarial clothing, validating its effectiveness in real-world scenarios across diverse distances, angles and backgrounds.

AI.tldr: AdvTiles is a physical adversarial camouflage framework that uses learnable tiles with a Straight-through Gumbel-Softmax estimator to jointly optimize tile patterns and spatial layouts, achieving strong attack performance (86.2% ASR) while preserving natural camouflage appearance, validated in both simulation and real-world wearable clothing.
AI.motivation: Existing physical adversarial attacks against person detectors face a trade-off between visual naturalness and attack effectiveness. Current natural-looking methods optimize camouflage textures holistically, which limits the ability to refine local adversarial patterns and their spatial arrangement.
AI.method: AdvTiles builds adversarial camouflage from learnable tiles. A Straight-through Gumbel-Softmax estimator enables differentiable tile selection for joint optimization of tile patterns and spatial layouts, providing fine-grained control over texture generation. The camouflage is further optimized through differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering with variations in viewpoints, scales, illuminations, and backgrounds to improve physical robustness.
AI.result: AdvTiles achieves an average Attack Success Rate (ASR) of 86.2% across multiple detectors, outperforming state-of-the-art attack methods. The optimized camouflage was fabricated into wearable adversarial clothing and validated in real-world scenarios across diverse distances, angles, and backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: The tile-based framework with joint optimization of patterns and layouts effectively combines visual naturalness with strong adversarial attack effectiveness, and the 3D Gaussian Splatting-based robust optimization enables successful transfer to physical-world wearable applications.

title: Bend the Basics: Degradation-Aware Deformable Tokenization for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: All-in-one image restoration seeks a single model that can recover images degraded by diverse and spatially non-uniform corruptions. However, many unified Transformers rely on fixed patch partitioning: task/degradation condition is injected only into the backbone blocks after tokenization, leaving the embedding and reconstruction stages insensitive to local degradation variations. In contrast to previous approaches, we present Flexible Image Transformer (FIT) that explicitly models degradation awareness across the entire pipeline, from patch sampling to pixel reconstruction. Specifically, FIT employs a lightweight Degradation Encoder to predict a global degradation vector $\mathbf{g}$ and a spatial degradation map $\mathbf{M}$ from local degradation severity, which jointly condition the patch embedding and unembedding through adaptive deformation. Moreover, to improve robustness across degradation types, we introduce a task-token dropout strategy that regularizes task conditioning during training. On five standard benchmarks (BSD68, Rain100L, SOTS, GoPro, and LOLv1), FIT achieves state-of-the-art performance with 30.72 dB average PSNR on the five-degradation setting and 32.83 dB on the three-degradation setting, outperforming recent unified restoration methods by +0.5$\sim$1.1 dB. Moreover, the learned offsets provide a direct handle for visualizing degradation-aware spatial adaptation.

AI.tldr: FIT is a unified image restoration Transformer that explicitly models degradation awareness throughout the entire pipeline—from patch sampling via a Degradation Encoder conditioning both embedding and unembedding, achieving state-of-the-art performance on five benchmarks with +0.5~1.1 dB over prior unified methods.
AI.motivation: Existing unified image restoration Transformers use fixed patch partitioning and inject task/degradation conditions only into backbone blocks after tokenization, leaving embedding and reconstruction stages insensitive to local degradation variations. This limits their ability to handle diverse and spatially non-uniform corruptions.
AI.method: FIT introduces a lightweight Degradation Encoder that predicts a global degradation vector g and a spatial degradation map M from local degradation severity. These jointly condition patch embedding and unembedding through adaptive deformation. A task-token dropout strategy is also proposed to regularize task conditioning during training and improve robustness across degradation types.
AI.result: FIT achieves 30.72 dB average PSNR on the five-degradation setting and 32.83 dB on the three-degradation setting, outperforming recent unified restoration methods by +0.5~1.1 dB across BSD68, Rain100L, SOTS, GoPro, and LOLv1 benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: FIT demonstrates that degradation-aware conditioning across the full pipeline (not just the backbone) improves unified image restoration. The learned offsets also provide a direct handle for visualizing degradation-aware spatial adaptation, offering interpretability.

title: GOPI: Generation-Oriented 3D Pose Inference for Furniture Insertion from Single-View RGB-D Indoor Scenes
summary:
We study the problem of inserting new furniture into indoor scene images. Under masked single-view 2D image-plane conditioning, however, the physical scale of the inserted furniture relative to the scene cannot be uniquely determined, making physically grounded furniture placement underdetermined from image evidence alone. We therefore reformulate the task as a combination of 3D pose inference and geometry-guided image generation, where estimating a geometrically plausible 3D placement is essential for reliable synthesis.
  To this end, we propose a two-stage framework. For 3D placement, we introduce GOPI, a generation-oriented 3D pose inference framework that addresses the underdetermined nature of single-view furniture insertion through data-driven iterative inference, producing geometrically plausible object placements. For image generation, we develop a geometry-guided conditioning strategy that projects the inferred 3D pose into the image plane as a pixel-aligned constraint, enforcing consistency between the synthesized image and the underlying 3D geometry.
  Experimental results validate the proposed framework from both 3D pose estimation and image synthesis perspectives. For 3D placement, GOPI produces poses with stronger geometric feasibility and better consistency with reference layouts than direct regression and vanilla baselines. For image synthesis, our method preserves alignment with the projected 3D geometry across different furniture scales, showing stable projection-generation alignment across the tested furniture scales.

AI.tldr: This paper tackles furniture insertion into indoor scene images by reformulating the task as 3D pose inference followed by geometry-guided image generation. A two-stage framework is proposed: GOPI, a generation-oriented 3D pose inference framework using data-driven iterative inference to handle the underdetermined placement problem, and a geometry-guided conditioning strategy that projects the inferred 3D pose into the image plane for pixel-aligned synthesis constraints. Experiments show improved geometric feasibility in 3D placement and stable projection-generation alignment across furniture scales.
AI.motivation: The physical scale of inserted furniture relative to a scene cannot be uniquely determined from single-view 2D image-plane conditioning, making physically grounded furniture placement underdetermined. To address this ambiguity, a framework that combines 3D pose inference with geometry-guided image generation is needed.
AI.method: A two-stage framework: (1) GOPI, a generation-oriented 3D pose inference framework using data-driven iterative inference to produce geometrically plausible object placements under the underdetermined single-view setting; (2) a geometry-guided conditioning strategy that projects the inferred 3D pose into the image plane as pixel-aligned constraints to ensure consistency between the synthesized image and the underlying 3D geometry.
AI.result: For 3D placement, GOPI produces poses with stronger geometric feasibility and better consistency with reference layouts than direct regression and vanilla baselines. For image synthesis, the method preserves alignment with the projected 3D geometry across different furniture scales, demonstrating stable projection-generation alignment.
AI.conclusion: The proposed two-stage framework effectively addresses the underdetermined nature of single-view furniture insertion, achieving both geometrically plausible 3D placements and consistent image synthesis across various furniture scales.

title: ECAD: Expanding Class-Agnostic Detection Beyond Thing-Centric Objectness
summary: Object detection is a fundamental task in visual perception, providing structured region representations for recognition, grounding, reasoning, and interaction. However, existing detection paradigms largely inherit a thing-centric notion of objectness, where detectors are mainly trained to localize discrete and countable object instances. Consequently, many semantically meaningful visual elements, such as sky, road, grassland, water, and sports courts, are often absorbed into the background despite their importance for scene understanding and spatial reasoning. In this paper, we formulate Expanded Class-Agnostic Detection (ECAD), a new setting that aims to discover category-agnostic visual candidates beyond conventional thing-centric objects.
