To support this setting, we construct BTCO-Bench, a Beyond Thing-Centric Objectness benchmark with category-agnostic box annotations covering both real-world and cross-domain scenarios. We further propose ECADet, a lightweight DETR-based detector built upon a frozen DINOv3 encoder, and introduce Geometry-Aware Expert Regression (GAER) and Prototype-Guided Query Modulation (PGQM) to improve localization and objectness estimation for diverse visual elements, respectively. Extensive experiments show that ECADet consistently outperforms representative class-agnostic and proposal-based detectors on BTCO-Bench, demonstrating the effectiveness of expanded objectness discovery. Code and benchmark will be released.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Expanded Class-Agnostic Detection (ECAD), a new setting for discovering category-agnostic visual candidates beyond conventional thing-centric objects, along with a benchmark (BTCO-Bench), a lightweight detector (ECADet), and two novel components (GAER and PGQM) that improve localization and objectness estimation for diverse visual elements such as sky, roads, and sports courts.
AI.motivation: Existing object detection paradigms are thing-centric, focusing on discrete and countable objects, which causes semantically meaningful visual elements (e.g., sky, road, grassland, water) to be treated as background despite their importance for scene understanding and spatial reasoning.
AI.method: The paper formulates ECAD as a new detection setting, constructs BTCO-Bench with category-agnostic box annotations across real-world and cross-domain scenarios, and proposes ECADet—a lightweight DETR-based detector built on a frozen DINOv3 encoder—incorporating Geometry-Aware Expert Regression (GAER) for improved localization and Prototype-Guided Query Modulation (PGQM) for better objectness estimation.
AI.result: ECADet consistently outperforms representative class-agnostic and proposal-based detectors on BTCO-Bench, demonstrating the effectiveness of expanded objectness discovery.
AI.conclusion: The proposed ECAD setting, benchmark, and detector effectively expand object detection beyond thing-centric objects, enabling the discovery of background-like visual elements that are crucial for comprehensive scene understanding. Code and benchmark will be released.

title: RegionDet: A Benchmark for Region Detection Beyond Object Instances
summary: Object detection is a fundamental task in computer vision and has achieved remarkable progress on standard benchmarks by localizing discrete and well-bounded object instances. However, many visual targets in real-world scenarios are not individual objects, but regions defined by visual states, scene context, object relations, and human activities, such as construction areas, damaged road regions, queues, group conversations, and vendor regions. Existing detection benchmarks are mainly built around object instances, providing limited support for systematically evaluating such region targets. To address this gap, we introduce Region Detection, a task that extends conventional object detection beyond object instances, and construct RegionDet, a benchmark for region target localization. RegionDet contains eight region categories, including Construction, Crossing, Damage, Queuing, Talking, Vendor, Waiting, and Walking, with COCO-style bounding-box annotations and evaluation protocols. We systematically evaluate representative closed-set and zero-shot/open-vocabulary detectors on RegionDet. Results show that closed-set detectors can partially learn region-level patterns under supervision, while zero-shot/open-vocabulary detectors struggle severely, revealing the strong object-centric bias of current vision-language detectors. Further analyses highlight key challenges in Region Detection, including weak boundary cues, strong context dependency, and insufficient relation-level region understanding. The RegionDet will be released.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Region Detection, a new task extending conventional object detection to localization of region targets (e.g., construction areas, queues, group conversations) defined by visual states, scene context, object relations, and human activities. The authors construct RegionDet, a benchmark with eight region categories and COCO-style annotations, showing that closed-set detectors partially learn region patterns while zero-shot/open-vocabulary detectors struggle severely due to object-centric bias.
AI.motivation: Existing object detection benchmarks focus on discrete, well-bounded object instances and provide limited support for evaluating region targets that are defined by visual states, scene context, object relations, and human activities rather than individual object identities.
AI.method: The authors define the Region Detection task, build the RegionDet benchmark containing eight region categories (Construction, Crossing, Damage, Queuing, Talking, Vendor, Waiting, Walking) with COCO-style bounding-box annotations and evaluation protocols, and systematically evaluate representative closed-set and zero-shot/open-vocabulary detectors on it.
AI.result: Closed-set detectors can partially learn region-level patterns under supervision, while zero-shot/open-vocabulary detectors struggle severely, revealing a strong object-centric bias in current vision-language detectors. Key challenges include weak boundary cues, strong context dependency, and insufficient relation-level region understanding.
AI.conclusion: Region Detection presents a new benchmarking direction beyond object instances, exposing limitations of existing detectors for region-level targets and highlighting the need for better relation-level and context-aware understanding in detection systems.

title: Multi-Agent Forensic Reasoning for Generalizable Deepfake Video Detection
summary: The malicious use of generative artificial intelligence to create highly realistic deepfake videos raises serious ethical concerns and poses substantial challenges to AI safety. However, existing deepfake video benchmarks provide limited coverage of recent synthesis methods and generally lack reliable fine-grained textual annotations. Meanwhile, conventional detectors and multimodal large language models (MLLMs), whether operating as a single model or relying on a single analytical perspective, often fail to capture subtle forgery artifacts, limiting their generalization to emerging AI-generated methods. To address these limitations, we introduce FaceVid-Forensics-100K, a large-scale deepfake video dataset comprising 100,000 videos and spanning 33 synthesis methods across face swapping, face reenactment, and entire-face synthesis, including recent generators such as Seedance 2.0. The dataset provides fine-grained textual annotations of visual observations and verdict-consistent forensic explanations, automatically synthesized through a multi-model aggregation and conflict-resolution pipeline powered by advanced MLLMs. Building on this benchmark, we propose a multi-agent forensic reasoning framework that employs four specialized domain-expert agents to independently analyze forgery cues from four perspectives: texture, lighting, motion, and physics. A judge agent then reconciles their reports to produce a final prediction together with an explanation. Extensive evaluations on out-of-domain test sets show that, despite being composed entirely of small open-source MLLMs, our framework outperforms all methods including closed-source GPT and Gemini models and ranks first across all reported metrics on this benchmark. The project page is available at https://xavierjiezou.github.io/ARGUS/.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces FaceVid-Forensics-100K, a large-scale deepfake video dataset with 100,000 videos covering 33 synthesis methods and fine-grained textual annotations, along with a multi-agent forensic reasoning framework (ARGUS) using four domain-expert agents and a judge agent that outperforms closed-source MLLMs on out-of-domain benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing deepfake video benchmarks have limited coverage of recent synthesis methods and lack reliable fine-grained textual annotations. Conventional detectors and single-model MLLMs fail to capture subtle forgery artifacts and generalize poorly to emerging AI-generated methods, posing challenges to AI safety.
AI.method: The authors build FaceVid-Forensics-100K with 100,000 videos spanning 33 synthesis methods, annotated via a multi-model aggregation and conflict-resolution pipeline powered by advanced MLLMs. They propose a multi-agent forensic reasoning framework with four domain-expert agents analyzing texture, lighting, motion, and physics separately, followed by a judge agent that reconciles their reports for final predictions and explanations.
AI.result: On out-of-domain test sets, the framework composed entirely of small open-source MLLMs outperforms all baseline methods including closed-source GPT and Gemini models, ranking first across all reported metrics on this benchmark.
AI.conclusion: A multi-agent approach with specialized domain experts can effectively capture subtle forgery artifacts and generalize better than monolithic detectors or single MLLMs, demonstrating that small open-source models can surpass much larger closed-source systems when properly orchestrated.

title: DAEP: Difficulty-Aware Evidence Planning for Medical Video Corpus Temporal Answer Grounding
comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables, accepted by NLPCC 2026 Shared Task Track 3
summary: We describe DAEP, team BIGC's submission to NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 1 Track 3: Difficulty-Aware Temporal Answer Grounding in Video Corpus (DA-TAGVC). The task requires retrieving the target video from 50 candidates and localizing the answer-supporting span. DAEP ranks videos with subtitle, visual, and procedural-context evidence, expands high-scoring anchors into temporal spans, and reranks spans for final output. Its main design is to convert the task-provided simple/complex input label into an inference-time evidence plan controlling modality weights, Top-K aggregation, boundary threshold, expansion length, and reranking strength. In the official evaluation, BIGC ranks first among ten systems with an Average score of 0.2728. Validation ablations show that visual evidence, procedural context, and difficulty-aware planning improve ranking quality, with the largest gain on complex questions.

AI.tldr: DAEP is BIGC's top-ranked system (1st of 10, Average score 0.2728) for the NLPCC 2026 DA-TAGVC task, which converts a difficulty label into an inference-time evidence plan that controls modality weights, aggregation, boundaries, expansion, and reranking for temporal answer grounding in video corpora.
AI.motivation: The task of difficulty-aware temporal answer grounding in video corpora requires retrieving the correct video from 50 candidates and localizing the answer-supporting span, but simple and complex questions likely require different evidence strategies. The paper aims to leverage the task-provided difficulty label to dynamically plan inference.
AI.method: DAEP retrieves and ranks videos using subtitle, visual, and procedural-context evidence, expands high-scoring anchors into temporal spans, and reranks spans. The key innovation is mapping the simple/complex input label to an inference-time evidence plan that controls modality weights, Top-K aggregation, boundary threshold, expansion length, and reranking strength.
AI.result: BIGC ranks first among ten systems with an Average score of 0.2728 in the official evaluation. Validation ablations demonstrate that visual evidence, procedural context, and difficulty-aware planning improve ranking quality, with the largest gain on complex questions.
AI.conclusion: The difficulty-aware evidence planning is an effective design for temporal answer grounding, particularly benefiting complex questions, and contributes to state-of-the-art performance in the shared task.

title: FedVAR: Prototype-Aligned Federated Framework for Video Anomaly Recognition
summary: In the era of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising decentralized intelligence paradigm for Video Anomaly Recognition (VAR). This task is vital for maintaining high-fidelity Digital Twins and ensuring safety in mission-critical environments. However, the inherent data heterogeneity across distributed edge clients leads to a fundamental challenge known as semantic misalignment, where clients learn divergent feature representations of "normal" and "abnormal" events. The problem becomes particularly pronounced in VAR, where the presence of diverse and fine-grained anomaly categories leads each client to develop distinct semantic interpretations of abnormality. Existing federated methods primarily focus on binary anomaly detection and fail to address this misalignment, preventing effective fine-grained recognition. In this paper, we introduce FedVAR, a weakly-supervised FL framework explicitly designed for VAR. Leveraging the rich representations of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), FedVAR employs a prototype-based alignment mechanism that creates a shared semantic anchor for all clients to re-center and align their visual and textual feature spaces. This process enforces a consistent representation of "normality" across the decentralized network, directly mitigating semantic misalignment and enabling robust prompt-learning of anomaly direction vectors with minimal communication overhead. We conduct extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks under various non-IID data partitioning schemes, unseen domains, and novel anomaly classes. The results demonstrate that FedVAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated baselines, establishing a robust framework for distributed intelligence in video-based CPS.

AI.tldr: FedVAR is a weakly-supervised federated learning framework for Video Anomaly Recognition that uses prototype-based alignment with Vision-Language Models to mitigate semantic misalignment across distributed clients, enabling fine-grained anomaly recognition under data heterogeneity, unseen domains, and novel anomaly classes.
AI.motivation: In IIoT/CPS environments, federated learning for video anomaly recognition suffers from semantic misalignment—clients learn divergent representations of normal and abnormal events due to data heterogeneity and diverse fine-grained anomaly categories. Existing federated methods only handle binary detection and fail to address this misalignment for fine-grained recognition.
AI.method: FedVAR leverages Vision-Language Model representations and employs a prototype-based alignment mechanism that creates a shared semantic anchor across clients to re-center and align visual and textual feature spaces, enforcing consistent "normality" representation and enabling prompt-learning of anomaly direction vectors with minimal communication overhead.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on challenging benchmarks under various non-IID data partitioning schemes, unseen domains, and novel anomaly classes show FedVAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art federated baselines.
AI.conclusion: FedVAR establishes a robust framework for distributed intelligence in video-based Cyber-Physical Systems, effectively mitigating semantic misalignment and enabling fine-grained video anomaly recognition in federated settings.

title: ControlRef: Efficient Layout-Guided Multi-Instance Generation via Anchored 4D-RoPE
summary: Layout-guided multi-instance generation is essential for controllable image synthesis in Multi-Modal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiTs). However, integrating this capability into unified architectures remains challenging. Prior frameworks rely on redundant full-resolution canvas padding and Shifted-RoPE to manage multiple reference images. This mechanism drastically inflates computational overhead for sparse layouts and disrupts critical low-frequency RoPE features, creating a severe spatial-frequency compromise that blurs absolute spatial correspondence. To overcome these limitations, we propose ControlRef, a highly efficient and precise multi-instance synthesis framework. ControlRef utilizes a Unified Instance-Layout Control (UILC) attention mask to strictly decouple inter-instance semantic interactions and enforce precise regional binding. To further promote region-level spatial alignment, we introduce Anchored 4D-RoPE, a novel positional encoding mechanism that directly anchors tokens to their absolute geometric centers. By pre-aligning reference images to their corresponding bounding box resolutions, physically anchoring both layout and reference tokens to their absolute geometric centers, and stacking the references along the z-axis, Anchored 4D-RoPE natively preserves spatial priors and mitigates the spatial-frequency compromise without lossy shifting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ControlRef achieves state-of-the-art visual fidelity and localization accuracy, while concurrently slashing inference latency by over 80% in sparse layouts and reducing memory overhead by 50% in dense scenarios.

AI.tldr: ControlRef is an efficient multi-instance generation framework for MM-DiTs that uses a Unified Instance-Layout Control (UILC) attention mask and Anchored 4D-RoPE positional encoding to enable precise spatial control while reducing inference latency by over 80% in sparse layouts and memory overhead by 50% in dense scenarios.
AI.motivation: Prior frameworks use redundant full-resolution canvas padding and Shifted-RoPE for multi-instance generation, which inflates computational overhead for sparse layouts and disrupts low-frequency RoPE features, creating a spatial-frequency compromise that blurs absolute spatial correspondence.
AI.method: ControlRef introduces two key components: (1) a Unified Instance-Layout Control (UILC) attention mask that decouples inter-instance semantic interactions and enforces precise regional binding, and (2) Anchored 4D-RoPE, a novel positional encoding that anchors tokens to their absolute geometric centers by pre-aligning reference images to bounding box resolutions and stacking references along the z-axis, preserving spatial priors without lossy shifting.
AI.result: ControlRef achieves state-of-the-art visual fidelity and localization accuracy, while reducing inference latency by over 80% in sparse layouts and memory overhead by 50% in dense scenarios.
AI.conclusion: By natively preserving spatial priors and mitigating the spatial-frequency compromise, ControlRef demonstrates that highly efficient and precise multi-instance synthesis is achievable in unified MM-DiT architectures.

title: HazeSpikeMamba: Coupling Spiking-Inspired and State-Space Features for Self-Supervised Real-World Dehazing
summary: Dehazing networks are commonly trained on synthetic hazy-clear pairs, but their performance often drops on real photographs. Synthetic haze generated using the atmospheric scattering model does not fully capture the variability of real haze, and paired real hazy-clear images are scarce. In this work, we propose HazeSpikeMamba, a compact dehazing framework that combines a spiking-inspired local path and an attentive state-space global path in a multi-scale U-Net. The local path uses TPCNNSpike, a new spike-emission scheme inspired by the neighborhood coupling of Pulse-Coupled Neural Network (PCNN). Unlike grouped directional scanning, TPCNNSpike updates all neurons in parallel using the previous firing states of their Gaussian-weighted neighborhoods. The global path adapts the Attentive State-Space Module of MambaIRv2, retaining semantic prompting and sequence reordering while removing the window self-attention branch. Its state-space processing models long-range dependencies with complexity linear in sequence length. For target-domain adaptation, a frozen degradation network, pretrained on paired NH-HAZE data, re-synthesizes haze from the dehazed prediction. The reconstruction error updates only the final restoration layers of HazeSpikeMamba without haze-free labels during adaptation. A shared checkpoint is adapted once on each complete unlabeled target set, making the evaluation dataset-level and transductive rather than zero-shot or per-image optimization. The forward network contains 2.02M active parameters and requires 13.27G nominal MACs (measured with thop at 256x256 input). This adaptation consistently improves BRISQUE and NIMA on RTTS, URHI, and HSTS. On RTTS, BRISQUE decreases from 30.13 to 27.72 and NIMA increases from 4.13 to 4.87. Under this transductive protocol, the adapted model also achieves the best BRISQUE and NIMA on URHI and HSTS among the compared methods.

AI.tldr: HazeSpikeMamba is a compact dehazing framework combining a spiking-inspired local path (TPCNNSpike) and an attentive state-space global path in a multi-scale U-Net, with a transductive adaptation strategy using a frozen degradation network pretrained on NH-HAZE to re-synthesize haze from dehazed predictions without requiring paired real data. It achieves 2.02M active parameters and improves BRISQUE/NIMA metrics on RTTS, URHI, and HSTS.
AI.motivation: Dehazing networks trained on synthetic pairs often fail on real photographs because synthetic haze from atmospheric scattering models doesn't capture real-world variability, and paired real hazy-clear images are scarce.
AI.method: HazeSpikeMamba combines a local path using TPCNNSpike (a novel spike-emission scheme based on Pulse-Coupled Neural Network that updates all neurons in parallel using Gaussian-weighted neighborhood firing states) with a global path adapting the Attentive State-Space Module from MambaIRv2 (without window self-attention, achieving linear complexity). A frozen degradation network pretrained on NH-HAZE re-synthesizes haze from predictions, and the reconstruction error updates only final restoration layers without haze-free labels.
AI.result: On RTTS, BRISQUE improves from 30.13 to 27.72 and NIMA from 4.13 to 4.87. The adapted model achieves best BRISQUE and NIMA on URHI and HSTS among compared methods under the transductive protocol. The network has 2.02M active parameters and 13.27G MACs at 256x256 input.
AI.conclusion: The combination of spiking-inspired local processing and state-space global modeling, along with label-free transductive adaptation, effectively bridges the synthetic-to-real gap for image dehazing without requiring paired real data.

title: Prune Once: Retraining-Free Task-Agnostic Pruning for Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable generalization across diverse multimodal tasks through large-scale pre-training, yet their rapidly increasing computational and memory requirements pose significant challenges for deployment in constrained environments. Existing pruning strategies often depend on task-specific criteria or LLM-oriented importance measures, making them unsuitable for task-agnostic pruning, where no task-specific samples are available at pruning time and the pruned model remains broadly applicable. We introduce a retraining-free VLM pruning framework called PORTA that derives a task- and modality-agnostic importance formulation based on activation variation, estimated from generic calibration data, which reliably captures feature-level representation utility across modalities. PORTA further incorporates an adaptive sparsity allocation mechanism that assigns layer-wise pruning ratios based on output feature variability, avoiding the limitations of uniform sparsity and reducing performance degradation at high compression levels. Extensive experiments across VLM architectures, such as CLIP, BLIP, and Qwen2-VL, demonstrate that PORTA achieves competitive downstream performance under high sparsity without requiring any retraining, supporting efficient VLM compression. Code is available at https://github.com/cau-hai-lab/PORTA.git.

AI.tldr: PORTA is a retraining-free VLM pruning framework that uses activation variation from generic calibration data to derive task- and modality-agnostic importance scores, combined with adaptive layer-wise sparsity allocation based on output feature variability, achieving competitive performance under high sparsity across CLIP, BLIP, and Qwen2-VL without retraining.
AI.motivation: Existing VLM pruning methods rely on task-specific criteria or LLM-oriented importance measures, which fail for task-agnostic pruning where no task-specific samples are available at pruning time. The goal is to enable effective VLM compression in constrained environments without requiring retraining or task-specific data.
AI.method: PORTA derives a task- and modality-agnostic importance formulation based on activation variation estimated from generic calibration data, capturing feature-level representation utility across modalities. It also incorporates an adaptive sparsity allocation mechanism that assigns layer-wise pruning ratios based on output feature variability to avoid uniform sparsity limitations.
AI.result: Experiments across CLIP, BLIP, and Qwen2-VL demonstrate that PORTA achieves competitive downstream performance under high sparsity without retraining, supporting efficient VLM compression.
AI.conclusion: PORTA provides a practical, retraining-free solution for task-agnostic VLM pruning, enabling high compression with minimal performance degradation across diverse VLM architectures.

title: MuST-VAD: Mutual Structured Learning for Video Anomaly Detection
summary: In this paper, we propose MuST-VAD, a mutual structured learning framework for weakly supervised video anomaly detection (VAD) in which an anomaly detector and a large vision-language model (LVLM) exchange their acquired knowledge. Detectors in weakly supervised VAD learn anomaly scores from features extracted by a fixed, task-agnostic backbone. These fixed features bound the achievable detection accuracy. Recent methods therefore transfer LVLM semantics into the detector as richer features. However, this transfer is one-way: what the detector learns about the target videos never returns to the LVLM. MuST-VAD extends the one-way transfer into a bidirectional learning loop. In this loop, the latest detector predictions supervise the LVLM adaptation, and the adapted LVLM returns updated representations that retrain the detector; the two models alternate these updates over small video groups. Both models train on detector-selected key clips, while confidence weighting and annotation-anchored question answering keep the exchanged supervision reliable. On UCF-Crime, our mutual learning improves the one-pass transfer baseline from 88.15% to 88.63% AUROC and from 37.25% to 42.46% average precision (AP), outperforming the state-of-the-art method in AP by 4.13 points.

AI.tldr: MuST-VAD is a mutual structured learning framework for weakly supervised video anomaly detection that establishes a bidirectional learning loop between an anomaly detector and a large vision-language model (LVLM), where detector predictions supervise LVLM adaptation and adapted LVLM representations retrain the detector, improving AUROC from 88.15% to 88.63% and AP from 37.25% to 42.46% on UCF-Crime.
AI.motivation: Existing weakly supervised VAD methods rely on fixed, task-agnostic backbone features that limit detection accuracy. Recent approaches transfer LVLM semantics into the detector as richer features, but this transfer is one-way—knowledge learned by the detector never flows back to the LVLM, leaving potential improvements unexploited.
AI.method: MuST-VAD establishes a bidirectional learning loop: the latest detector predictions supervise LVLM adaptation, and the adapted LVLM returns updated representations to retrain the detector. The two models alternate updates over small video groups, training on detector-selected key clips. Confidence weighting and annotation-anchored question answering ensure reliable exchanged supervision.
AI.result: On UCF-Crime, mutual learning improves the one-pass transfer baseline from 88.15% to 88.63% AUROC and from 37.25% to 42.46% average precision (AP), outperforming the state-of-the-art method in AP by 4.13 points.
AI.conclusion: Bidirectional knowledge exchange between a detector and an LVLM yields measurable improvements over one-way transfer, demonstrating the value of mutual structured learning for weakly supervised video anomaly detection.

title: RibAssist 3D: Biplanar Rib-Fracture Detection, Addressing, and Selective 3D Localization from CT-Derived Projections
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures. Code available at: https://github.com/kabJhai/RibAssist-3D
summary: Rib fractures are common, clinically significant, and time-consuming to localize on computed tomography (CT). We ask whether fractures detected in two orthogonal projections (anteroposterior, AP, and lateral) can be paired across views and triangulated into reliable 3D fracture points at a controlled rate of false 3D outputs. We answer this with a staged diagnostic study. Biplanar geometry is exact: detector-predicted centers reconstruct to median 4.0 mm 3D error when correspondence is correct. On the sealed cohort, dual-view availability reaches 61.1% and the candidate graph contains a correct pair for 58.4% of fractures. The binding limitation is not geometry or localization but confidence-limited cross-view correspondence. Lateral-detector retraining lifts dual-view availability (0.52 to 0.76 in development) and moves the frontier from 0% to 2.44% recall at 10 mm. When the policy commits a correct pair, the emitted point is geometrically accurate (sealed median 1.49 mm, rib-exact 93%). A pre-specified pass on the untouched 55-case cohort promotes 15 of 601 fractures to correct 3D localizations at 0.436 false 3D points per case, yielding 2.50% end-to-end commitment yield. The contribution is validated biplanar reconstruction geometry with high conditional localization fidelity, a staged identification of cross-view correspondence confidence as the effective bottleneck, and a selective assistive workflow that preserves uncertain findings rather than a standalone automatic reconstructor.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a staged diagnostic study for detecting and localizing rib fractures on CT using biplanar (AP + lateral) projections, where fracture centers detected in both views are triangulated into 3D points with controlled false-output rates. Cross-view correspondence is identified as the key bottleneck rather than geometry; a selective workflow yields 2.50% end-to-end commitment yield with high conditional localization accuracy (median 1.49 mm, 93% rib-exact).
AI.motivation: Rib fracture localization on CT is time-consuming and clinically important. The authors investigate whether fractures detected in two orthogonal projections can be reliably paired across views and triangulated into accurate 3D locations, aiming for a selective assistive tool rather than a fully automatic system.
AI.method: A staged diagnostic study using biplanar geometry (anteroposterior and lateral projections) to triangulate detector-predicted fracture centers into 3D points. Candidate graphs are built for cross-view pairing, and a selective policy commits only when correspondence confidence is high, evaluated on a sealed 55-case cohort.
AI.result: Biplanar reconstruction achieves median 4.0 mm 3D error when correspondence is correct. Dual-view availability is 61.1% on the sealed cohort (58.4% correct pairs in candidate graph). Retraining the lateral detector raises availability from 0.52 to 0.76 and recall-at-10mm from 0% to 2.44%. Committed correct pairs yield median 1.49 mm error with 93% rib-exactness. The pass on 55 cases promotes 15 of 601 fractures at 0.436 false 3D points per case (2.50% end-to-end commitment yield).
AI.conclusion: Validated biplanar reconstruction geometry with high conditional localization fidelity is achievable, and the effective bottleneck is confidence-limited cross-view correspondence. A selective assistive workflow that preserves uncertain findings is more appropriate than a standalone automatic reconstructor for clinical deployment.

title: Vernata: Self-Supervised Learning of LiDAR Point Representations
summary: LiDAR serves as a primary sensing modality for robots operating in outdoor environments. However, the performance of deep learning models in this domain is severely limited by the scarcity of labeled data, a direct result of the high cost of 3D annotation. Self-supervised learning addresses this scarcity by learning general-purpose features from unlabeled data. In this work, we present a multi-modal, multi-teacher distillation framework for self-supervised learning on outdoor LiDAR point clouds. Building upon the Sonata architecture, we introduce Vernata, consisting of three extensions: sparse view augmentation to improve robustness against varying point densities, a memory bank mechanism to stabilize resource-constrained training, and cross-modal distillation utilizing dense, high-resolution 2D image features to enable fine-grained semantic guidance. We evaluate our method on the GrandTour, TartanGround, and Waymo datasets, as well as data collected from our own robotic platforms. Our experiments demonstrate a significant performance improvement over Sonata baselines, yielding mIoU scores of 54.7 on TartanGround (+5.9 points, +12.1%) and 57.1 on Waymo (+7.3 points, +14.7%). Finally, we show that the self-supervised approach maintains strong performance even in reduced-modality settings (lacking color or normals), achieving competitive mIoU scores of 49.4 and 50.2 on the respective datasets.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Vernata, a multi-modal, multi-teacher distillation framework for self-supervised learning on outdoor LiDAR point clouds, building on the Sonata architecture with three extensions: sparse view augmentation, a memory bank mechanism, and cross-modal distillation from 2D images. It achieves significant mIoU improvements over Sonata baselines on TartanGround (54.7, +12.1%) and Waymo (57.1, +14.7%) datasets, and maintains competitive performance even when color or normals are unavailable.
AI.motivation: Deep learning models on outdoor LiDAR point clouds are severely limited by the scarcity of labeled data due to the high cost of 3D annotation. Self-supervised learning offers a way to learn general-purpose features from unlabeled data, but existing approaches need improvement in robustness and semantic guidance for outdoor environments.
AI.method: Vernata extends the Sonata architecture with three key components: (1) sparse view augmentation to improve robustness against varying point densities, (2) a memory bank mechanism to stabilize resource-constrained training, and (3) cross-modal distillation that leverages dense, high-resolution 2D image features to enable fine-grained semantic guidance. This forms a multi-modal, multi-teacher distillation framework for self-supervised learning on outdoor LiDAR point clouds.
AI.result: Evaluation on GrandTour, TartanGround, and Waymo datasets plus custom robot data shows significant improvements over Sonata baselines: mIoU of 54.7 on TartanGround (+5.9 points, +12.1%) and 57.1 on Waymo (+7.3 points, +14.7%). In reduced-modality settings (lacking color or normals), the method achieves competitive mIoU scores of 49.4 and 50.2 on the respective datasets.
AI.conclusion: The self-supervised Vernata framework significantly outperforms Sonata baselines and demonstrates robustness in reduced-modality scenarios, indicating that multi-modal distillation from 2D image features and architectural improvements can effectively address labeling scarcity in outdoor LiDAR point cloud learning.

title: MaskFlow: Precise, Consistent and Seamless Regional Image Editing
summary: Regional image editing has attracted considerable attention for its spatial controllability. Although instruction-based and mask-reference-based editing methods can achieve strong semantic alignment, reliable regional control remains challenging, where an edit must be accurately localized and naturally integrated with the preserved context. We propose \textbf{MaskFlow}, a training framework for precise localization, consistent background preservation, and seamless boundary transitions. MaskFlow incorporates the mask into the probability path and flow-matching objective, coordinating generation within the editable region with source preservation outside it. The proposed Soft-Poisson de-seaming module further refines the predicted vector field during both training and sampling to improve the smooth integration of the edited foreground with the preserved background. We also design a data synthesis pipeline to construct MEData, a mask-based image editing dataset for training regional image editing models and facilitating further research. Experiments on natural scenes and infographic images demonstrate consistent improvements over competing methods in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

AI.tldr: MaskFlow is a training framework for regional image editing that incorporates masks into the flow-matching objective for precise localization, preserves backgrounds, and uses a Soft-Poisson de-seaming module for seamless boundary integration, along with a new MEData dataset.
AI.motivation: Existing regional image editing methods (instruction-based and mask-reference-based) achieve semantic alignment but struggle with reliable regional control—edits must be accurately localized while seamlessly integrating with preserved context.
AI.method: MaskFlow incorporates the mask into the probability path and flow-matching objective to coordinate generation inside editable regions with source preservation outside. A Soft-Poisson de-seaming module refines the predicted vector field during training and sampling for smooth foreground-background integration. A data synthesis pipeline constructs the MEData dataset for training.
AI.result: Experiments on natural scenes and infographic images show consistent improvements over competing methods in both quantitative and qualitative evaluations.
AI.conclusion: MaskFlow provides precise localization, consistent background preservation, and seamless boundary transitions for regional image editing, validated across diverse image domains.

title: AVCap: Reinforcing Audio-Video Joint Caption with Detail-Aware Reward
summary: Detailed audio-video joint captioning is essential for multimodal video understanding and generation. However, prior works are constrained by three main limitations: (1) the scarcity of high-quality public datasets with fine-grained audio-visual joint captions; (2) reinforcement-learning methods that rely on coarse reward signals; and (3) the lack of a benchmark and metric for evaluating detailed audiovisual captions at the atomic level. To address these challenges, we propose: (1) AVCap-100K, a high-quality dataset of 100K temporally aligned, detail-rich audio-video captions; (2) AVCap, a model optimized via Detail-Aware GRPO (Da-GRPO) that achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models and matches or surpasses proprietary models on several evaluations; and (3) AVCap-Bench and AVCap-Score, a specialized benchmark and metric for evaluating atomic-level details in audiovisual captions. Our code, models, and datasets are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Apryle/avcap.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces AVCap-100K (a dataset of 100K temporally aligned, detailed audio-video captions), AVCap (a model optimized via Detail-Aware GRPO achieving SOTA among open-source models), and AVCap-Bench/AVCap-Score (a benchmark and metric for atomic-level audiovisual caption evaluation).
AI.motivation: Detailed audio-video joint captioning is essential for multimodal understanding but prior works suffer from: (1) scarcity of high-quality public datasets with fine-grained audio-visual captions; (2) RL methods relying on coarse reward signals; (3) lack of a benchmark and metric for atomic-level detail evaluation.
AI.method: The paper proposes three components: (1) AVCap-100K dataset with 100K temporally aligned detail-rich audio-video captions; (2) AVCap model optimized via Detail-Aware GRPO (Da-GRPO); (3) AVCap-Bench and AVCap-Score for evaluating atomic-level details in audiovisual captions.
AI.result: AVCap achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models and matches or surpasses proprietary models on several evaluations.
AI.conclusion: The paper addresses gaps in audiovisual joint captioning through comprehensive dataset, model, and evaluation contributions, with resources made publicly available.

title: Debias in Text, Believe Your Eyes: Text-Anchored Cross-Modal Transfer for Visual Counter-Commonsense Reasoning
summary: The visual reasoning ability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) is crucial for downstream applications, particularly counter-commonsense reasoning, which requires models to reason beyond common assumptions. Recent studies mainly improve visual counter-commonsense reasoning by enhancing visual inputs, following the assumption that failures originate from insufficient visual grounding. However, our empirical analysis reveals that the bottleneck is not visual perception. MLLMs already capture the relevant visual evidence, and the correct answer exists in their decoding space. Instead, the shared language decoder resolves prior--evidence conflicts by favoring dominant language priors, especially for low-frequency factual scenarios. Motivated by this, we first propose a text-anchored data construction pipeline, whose core component, Fact-Frequency Distillation (FFD), estimates the prior strength of commonsense facts and distills verified counter-commonsense scenarios into a high-quality text corpus. Building upon this corpus, we introduce TACT, a text-anchored post-training framework that debiases the shared language decoder without requiring any visual training data. TACT routes evidence-following and prior-driven reasoning trajectories into different optimization stages, enabling the decoder to resolve prior--evidence conflicts. Across counter-commonsense visual benchmarks, TACT substantially improves visual reasoning while preserving general capabilities, demonstrating effective text-to-vision cross-modal transfer.

AI.tldr: The paper reveals that failures in visual counter-commonsense reasoning by MLLMs stem not from insufficient visual perception but from the shared language decoder favoring dominant language priors over visual evidence. The authors propose TACT, a text-anchored post-training framework that debiases the decoder using a text corpus distilled via Fact-Frequency Distillation (FFD), achieving substantial improvements on counter-commonsense visual benchmarks without visual training data.
AI.motivation: Visual counter-commonsense reasoning in MLLMs is important but underperforms. Prior work assumed failures come from insufficient visual grounding and focused on enhancing visual inputs. The authors challenge this assumption through empirical analysis.
AI.method: (1) Empirical analysis showing the bottleneck is the language decoder, not visual perception—MLLMs already capture visual evidence and the correct answer exists in decoding space. (2) A text-anchored data construction pipeline with Fact-Frequency Distillation (FFD) to estimate commonsense prior strength and build a high-quality counter-commonsense text corpus. (3) TACT, a text-anchored post-training framework that debiases the shared language decoder by routing evidence-following and prior-driven reasoning trajectories into different optimization stages, requiring no visual training data.
AI.result: TACT substantially improves visual counter-commonsense reasoning across benchmarks while preserving general capabilities, demonstrating effective text-to-vision cross-modal transfer.
AI.conclusion: The root cause of counter-commonsense reasoning failures lies in the language decoder's bias toward language priors, and this can be corrected through text-only post-training, enabling cross-modal transfer to visual reasoning tasks.

title: Degradation-Aware Prompt Learning with Cross-Modal Compensation for Adverse Weather Removal
comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Image Processing. The code is available at: https://github.com/fanamber831/DCMPC-Net
summary: Adverse weather causes diverse and complex image degradations, severely compromising the reliability of computer vision systems. Existing all-in-one restoration models attempt to address multiple degradation types within a unified framework, but often lack explicit spatial and semantic modeling of degradation characteristics, limiting their adaptability to diverse weather conditions. To address this limitation, we propose a Degradation-Aware Cross-Modal Prompt Compensation Network (DCMPC-Net) that leverages cross-modal degradation cues from a pretrained vision-language model to condition restoration features within a unified backbone. Specifically, our DCMPC-Net mainly consists of the Cross-Modal Prompt Generator (CMPG), Prompt-Guided Attention Alignment Module (PGAAM), and Dual Feature Compensation Module (DFCM). The CMPG integrates textual embeddings with visual features to produce degradation-aware prompts that encode degradation-related semantic and contextual cues. These prompts are injected into the decoder via a PGAAM, which adaptively aligns semantic information with degraded regions to facilitate context-aware restoration. To further enhance structural fidelity, DFCM is introduced that disentangles degradation artifacts from scene structures, thereby improving the reconstruction of fine textures and detailed content. By integrating cross-modal semantic guidance with spatial alignment and structural enhancement, DCMPC-Net achieves robust and perceptually consistent restoration across diverse weather conditions. Extensive experiments show that DCMPC-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both task-specific and unified settings, achieving superior accuracy and visual fidelity.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes DCMPC-Net, a unified all-in-one image restoration model that handles diverse adverse weather conditions (rain, snow, haze, etc.) by leveraging cross-modal degradation cues from a pretrained vision-language model. The model integrates three key modules—Cross-Modal Prompt Generator (CMPG), Prompt-Guided Attention Alignment Module (PGAAM), and Dual Feature Compensation Module (DFCM)—to incorporate degradation-aware semantic prompts, spatial alignment, and feature compensation for robust restoration.
AI.motivation: Existing all-in-one restoration models handle multiple degradation types in a unified framework but typically lack explicit spatial and semantic modeling of degradation characteristics, which limits their adaptability across diverse weather conditions.
AI.method: The DCMPC-Net uses a pretrained vision-language model to extract cross-modal degradation cues. Three main components: (1) CMPG integrates textual embeddings with visual features to generate degradation-aware prompts; (2) PGAAM injects these prompts into the decoder to align semantic information with degraded regions; (3) DFCM disentangles degradation artifacts from scene structures to enhance structural fidelity and fine texture reconstruction.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate that DCMPC-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both task-specific and unified restoration settings, achieving superior accuracy and visual fidelity.
AI.conclusion: By combining cross-modal semantic guidance with spatial alignment and structural enhancement, DCMPC-Net achieves robust and perceptually consistent restoration across diverse weather conditions.

title: Dual-Space Modality Consistency Learning for Universal Cross-Modal Re-Identification
summary: Cross-modal Re-Identification (ReID) aims to retrieve the same identity across heterogeneous imaging modalities and has been widely studied in visible-infrared person ReID and cross-modal ship ReID. Existing methods have achieved promising performance by learning modality consistency in the spatial embedding space, yet often overlook frequency-domain modality discrepancy, particularly in high-frequency representations that are both highly discriminative and modality-sensitive. In addition, most approaches are tailored to specific modality settings, limiting their applicability across diverse cross-modal scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a Dual-Space Modality Consistency Learning (DSMCL) framework for universal cross-modal ReID. Specifically, DSMCL jointly models spatial feature distribution consistency and frequency-domain discriminative consistency. A Spatial Modality Consistency Learning (SMCL) branch performs Gaussian-based feature alignment, while a Frequency-aware Discriminative Consistency Learning (FDCL) strategy regularizes high-frequency representations through identity-aware cross-modal contrastive learning. By jointly capturing modality-specific characteristics and modality-shared identity cues, DSMCL learns robust representations and establishes a unified framework capable of accommodating diverse heterogeneous modality settings. Moreover, DSMCL is a plug-and-play framework that can be readily integrated into existing cross-modal ReID architectures. Extensive experiments on SYSU-MM01, RegDB, LLCM, HOSS-ReID, and CMShipReID across seventeen evaluation protocols show that DSMCL consistently improves multiple representative baselines.

AI.tldr: DSMCL is a plug-and-play framework for universal cross-modal Re-Identification that jointly models spatial feature distribution consistency and frequency-domain discriminative consistency, improving multiple baselines across five benchmarks and seventeen evaluation protocols.
AI.motivation: Existing cross-modal ReID methods focus on spatial embedding space consistency but overlook frequency-domain modality discrepancies, especially in high-frequency representations that are both discriminative and modality-sensitive. Additionally, most methods are tailored to specific modality settings, limiting generality.
AI.method: A Dual-Space Modality Consistency Learning framework with two branches: (1) Spatial Modality Consistency Learning (SMCL) for Gaussian-based feature alignment, and (2) Frequency-aware Discriminative Consistency Learning (FDCL) that regularizes high-frequency representations via identity-aware cross-modal contrastive learning. The framework is plug-and-play for existing cross-modal ReID architectures.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on SYSU-MM01, RegDB, LLCM, HOSS-ReID, and CMShipReID across seventeen evaluation protocols show consistent improvement over multiple representative baselines.
AI.conclusion: By jointly capturing modality-specific and modality-shared identity cues in both spatial and frequency domains, DSMCL learns robust representations and establishes a unified framework applicable across diverse heterogeneous modality settings.

title: Summarize First, Download Later: Onboard VLMs for Bandwidth-Efficient Earth Observation
summary: Modern Earth observation (EO) satellites carry increasingly advanced sensors that produce vast volumes of high-resolution, multispectral data, yet downlink capacity remains a critical bottleneck -- often causing significant latency or the loss of valuable observations within limited contact windows. We propose a "Summarize First, Download Later" paradigm that exploits recent advances in onboard edge computing and Vision-Language Models (VLMs). Rather than indiscriminately downlinking raw imagery, the system follows a three-phase interaction protocol: the satellite first transmits concise natural language summaries generated by a quantized onboard VLM; ground operators then issue targeted Visual Question Answering (VQA) queries to verify scene relevance (e.g., wildfires or maritime anomalies); and full-resolution images are downloaded only when critical information is confirmed. This transforms the downlink from passive bulk transfer into an active, semantics-aware dialogue. We implement and evaluate the system on a resource-constrained NVIDIA Jetson platform, and experiments on diverse remote sensing scenes show that the proposed strategy substantially reduces bandwidth consumption while accelerating time-to-insight for time-sensitive missions.

AI.tldr: Proposes a "Summarize First, Download Later" paradigm for EO satellites that uses onboard quantized Vision-Language Models to generate text summaries of imagery, enables ground operators to query via VQA for scene verification, and downloads full-resolution images only when critical information is confirmed—reducing bandwidth and accelerating time-to-insight on a Jetson platform.
AI.motivation: Earth observation satellites collect massive volumes of high-resolution multispectral data, but downlink capacity is a critical bottleneck causing latency and data loss. The paper aims to transform downlink from passive bulk transfer to an active, semantics-aware dialogue to address this resource constraint.
AI.method: Implements a three-phase interaction protocol: (1) satellite generates concise natural language summaries via a quantized onboard VLM; (2) ground operators issue targeted VQA queries to verify scene relevance; (3) full-resolution images are downloaded only when critical information is confirmed. Evaluated on a resource-constrained NVIDIA Jetson platform.
AI.result: Experiments on diverse remote sensing scenes demonstrate the strategy substantially reduces bandwidth consumption while accelerating time-to-insight for time-sensitive missions.
AI.conclusion: Leveraging onboard edge computing and VLMs with a semantics-aware downlink protocol can significantly improve the efficiency of EO satellite communication, making it particularly valuable for time-critical applications like wildfire detection and maritime anomaly monitoring.

title: Generative Embedding Benchmark: How Much Information Survives in a Dense Embedding?
summary: Embeddings have emerged as a standard representational interface linking foundation models with downstream systems. Most embedding benchmarks assess representations through discriminative tasks or geometric criteria centered on separability in embedding space. However, strong performance on such evaluations does not establish whether content compressed into an embedding remains accessible to a downstream generator. To address this gap, we introduce the Generative Embedding Benchmark (GEB), in which a decoder answers questions using only a frozen embedding and question text, without access to the original image or intermediate visual features. Answer quality under this readout measures generative information: the answer-relevant content recoverable from an embedding. GEB includes a curated visual-question-answering dataset with a 1,800-item development split and a held-out 900-item test split covering natural images, scene text, and visual documents. Using a common decoder and training recipe, we evaluate seven public embedding models in visual-only and vision-language joint modes. On the test set, visual-only scores range from 28.25 to 33.21; with image-question joint encoding, all five VLM-based embedding models score higher, and the best reaches 65.56. Matched embeddings also outperform text-only inputs, zero embeddings, and shuffled embeddings. Natural-image information is much easier to recover than scene text or visual-document information, while a Qwen3-VL-2B reference with access to the original image reaches 84.30. Together, these results show that generative readout exposes information bottlenecks that separability-based evaluation does not capture.

AI.tldr: GEB is a new benchmark that evaluates whether content compressed in embeddings can be recovered by a generative decoder (answering VQA questions from frozen embeddings only). Results show large performance gaps between models (28–65 on test set), with VLM joint-encoding models performing best, and demonstrate that generative information recovery exposes bottlenecks not captured by separability-based benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing embedding benchmarks rely on discriminative tasks or geometric criteria (separability), but strong performance there does not guarantee that content stored in an embedding is accessible to downstream generative systems. There is a need for an evaluation that measures whether answer-relevant information can actually be recovered from an embedding.
AI.method: The authors introduce the Generative Embedding Benchmark (GEB): a decoder answers questions using only a frozen embedding plus question text, with no access to the original image or intermediate visual features. It includes a curated VQA dataset (1,800 dev items, 900 test items) covering natural images, scene text, and visual documents. Seven public embedding models are evaluated in visual-only and vision-language joint modes using a common decoder and training recipe.
AI.result: Visual-only scores range from 28.25 to 33.21 on the test set. With image-question joint encoding, all five VLM-based models score higher, with the best reaching 65.56. Matched embeddings outperform text-only inputs, zero embeddings, and shuffled embeddings. Natural-image information is much easier to recover than scene text or visual-document information. A Qwen3-VL-2B reference with original image access reaches 84.30.
AI.conclusion: Generative readout (answering questions from embeddings alone) exposes information bottlenecks that separability-based evaluation does not capture, making GEB a valuable complement to existing embedding benchmarks.

title: When One Modality Is Not Enough: Multimodal Sex and Life-Stage Classification of Red Deer from Aerial RGB-Thermal Video
comment: Accepted at the ECCV 2026 Workshop on Computer Vision for Ecology (CV4Ecology), archival proceedings track. 17 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables
summary: Aerial drone surveys increasingly support wildlife population estimation, yet a useful census is more than a count: population dynamics are defined by species composition, sex ratios and age structure, that is, by which species are present and how a herd splits into adult males, adult females and juveniles. We use red deer ($\textit{Cervus elaphus}$) as a test case, because managers act on these dynamics and because the visible cue defining adult males, the antlers, is seasonally variable. Surveys are flown nadir, high enough not to disturb the animals, so each deer occupies only a small, low-resolution patch. The two recording modalities fail in opposite conditions: in color a deer under canopy blends into the ground, while in thermal it becomes a bright blob that loses fine detail. Rather than trust either modality alone, we fuse them at every stage using self-supervised DINOv3 features. Our pipeline tracks animals in both modalities, treats an animal as confirmed only when the two cameras agree, keeps only the clear, non-occluded frames, and assigns species and sex by a vote across them; life stage is read separately from geo-referenced body size, since at survey resolution a juvenile often only differs from an adult female in size. Across four flights spanning the antler season the fused pipeline correctly classifies 25 of the 26 detected individuals (7 of 8 adult males, all 16 adult females and 2 juveniles), against 20 of 26 for either sensor alone. Multimodal species classification reaches 96.0%, while for sex classification fusing the two sensors matters most: the combined RGB+thermal model is the most robust across environments and seasons. Automating the demographic classification turns a drone flight from a count into a repeatable reading of herd structure, so the sex ratios and age structure that managers already act on can be gathered as often as a survey can be flown.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a multimodal fusion pipeline for aerial drone surveys that automatically classifies red deer demographics (species, sex, age) by fusing RGB and thermal imagery using self-supervised DINOv3 features. The system achieves 96% species classification accuracy and correctly classifies 25 of 26 detected individuals across four flights spanning the antler season, outperforming either sensor alone.
AI.motivation: Aerial drone surveys can count animals but a census requires demographic information (species composition, sex ratios, age structure) that managers act upon. However, individual RGB and thermal modalities fail in opposite conditions—RGB loses deer under canopy while thermal loses fine detail needed for sex classification (especially antlers, which vary seasonally).
AI.method: The pipeline fuses RGB and thermal modalities at every stage using self-supervised DINOv3 features. It tracks animals in both modalities, confirms an animal only when both cameras agree, keeps only clear non-occluded frames, and assigns species/sex by majority vote. Life stage (juvenile vs adult) is determined separately from geo-referenced body size since juveniles mainly differ from adult females in size at survey resolution.
AI.result: Across four flights spanning the antler season, the fused pipeline correctly classifies 25 of 26 detected individuals (7/8 adult males, all 16 adult females, and 2 juveniles), compared to 20 of 26 for either sensor alone. Multimodal species classification reaches 96.0%, and fused RGB+thermal is the most robust model for sex classification across environments and seasons.
AI.conclusion: Automating demographic classification transforms drone surveys from simple animal counts into repeatable readings of herd structure, enabling managers to gather sex ratios and age structure data as frequently as surveys can be flown.

title: Local Epistemic Uncertainty Guided Active Sampling for Plug-and-play Diffusive Image Restoration
comment: 12 Pages, 7 Figures, 5 Tables. Accepted to ACM Multimedia 2026
summary: Diffusion models have demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in image restoration tasks. However, when guiding image reconstruction, existing Diffusion Model-based Image Restoration (DMIR) methods typically rely on fixed data constraints and uniform step sizes, thereby overlooking the dynamic nature of the generative process. Such rigid designs render the models vulnerable to spatially non-uniform degradations, thus resulting in structural distortions and loss of fine details. Meanwhile, uniform step sizes introduce computational redundancy, whereas naïve step reduction strategies tend to accumulate approximation errors. To address these limitations, we propose a Local Epistemic Uncertainty Guided Active Sampling framework (LEADer). In the spatial domain, LEADer leverages pixel-wise uncertainty to dynamically modulate the prior strength within the null space, which effectively balances detail preservation and artifact suppression. In the temporal domain, it quantifies sampling stability via the uncertainty trace to enable adaptive trajectory pruning, thereby accelerating convergence. Theoretical proofs demonstrate that our framework achieves strict data consistency, while the trajectory pruning strategy admits a deterministic error bound, thereby guaranteeing stable convergence under skip sampling. Notably, our plug-and-play method can be seamlessly integrated into various DMIR baselines. Extensive experiments show that LEADer improves the performance of multiple state-of-the-art DMIR methods, while significantly reducing sampling time with negligible memory overhead. Code is available at https://github.com/JiaqiZhang-Sengoku/LEADer.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes LEADer, a plug-and-play framework for Diffusion Model-based Image Restoration (DMIR) that uses pixel-wise epistemic uncertainty to dynamically modulate prior strength in the spatial domain and uncertainty trace-based adaptive trajectory pruning in the temporal domain, improving performance and reducing sampling time.
AI.motivation: Existing DMIR methods use fixed data constraints and uniform step sizes during reconstruction, which overlooks the dynamic nature of the generative process. This makes them vulnerable to spatially non-uniform degradations (causing structural distortions and detail loss) and introduces computational redundancy in sampling steps.
AI.method: LEADer comprises two key components: (1) spatial-domain pixel-wise epistemic uncertainty that dynamically modulates prior strength within the null space to balance detail preservation and artifact suppression; (2) temporal-domain sampling stability quantification via uncertainty trace to enable adaptive trajectory pruning. Theoretical proofs establish strict data consistency and a deterministic error bound for trajectory pruning.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show LEADer improves the performance of multiple state-of-the-art DMIR baselines while significantly reducing sampling time with negligible memory overhead.
AI.conclusion: LEADer is an effective plug-and-play mechanism that can be seamlessly integrated into various DMIR baselines, achieving better restoration quality with faster convergence and no significant computational cost.

title: HRDiT: Training-Free High-Resolution Image Generation with Off-the-Shelf Diffusion Transformer Models
summary: Training-free text-to-high-resolution image generation has recently attracted growing research attention. However, existing studies on this task primarily focus on adapting off-the-shelf U-Net-based diffusion models to high resolutions, with limited progress on adapting off-the-shelf Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models despite their strong text-to-image generation capabilities at limited resolutions. In this work, we find two key challenges particularly hindering the application of off-the-shelf DiT models for high-resolution image synthesis in a training-free manner, namely, spatial disorder and long generation time. To address these challenges, we propose a novel method tailored to adapt off-the-shelf DiT models for high-resolution image synthesis. Extensive experiments show the efficacy of our method. Our code is available at: https://github.com/zylwithxy/HRDiT.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses training-free high-resolution image generation using off-the-shelf Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models, identifying two key challenges—spatial disorder and long generation time—and proposes a novel method (HRDiT) to overcome them, with code publicly available.
AI.motivation: While training-free high-resolution image generation has been explored, existing work primarily targets U-Net-based diffusion models. DiT models, despite strong text-to-image capabilities at limited resolutions, have not been effectively adapted for high-resolution synthesis, posing an open gap this paper aims to fill.
AI.method: The paper analyzes the challenges of spatial disorder and long generation time in applying off-the-shelf DiT models to high-resolution synthesis, then proposes a tailored training-free method to address these issues without requiring additional training.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method for high-resolution image synthesis with off-the-shelf DiT models.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method successfully enables training-free high-resolution image generation using DiT models, addressing spatial disorder and generation time challenges, with code released for reproducibility.

title: Scenix: Sparse-View 3D Scene Reconstruction via Executable Scene Programs
summary: Synthesizing a structured and editable 3D indoor scene from a few uncalibrated RGB views requires more than generating high-quality individual assets: a system must infer the room structure, associate objects across incomplete observations, and recover a globally consistent spatial configuration. Previous methods mainly focus on 3D scene generation with text input or require continuous visual inputs with additional priors, \ e.g., human-annotated masks or accurate 3D layouts, which makes these methods labor demanding and hard to apply in general cases. We present \textsc{Scenix}, a sparse-view 3D scene reconstruction framework via executable scene programs, a structured representation that can be directly instantiated into editable 3D scenes. Given sparse views, \textsc{Scenix} predicts executable scene programs through perception-grounded asset instantiation and closed-loop spatial refinement. % We present \method, a framework that predicts an executable scene representation from sparse views and realizes it through perception-grounded asset instantiation and closed-loop spatial refinement. To support this task, we construct \dataset, a dataset of approximately 110,000 synthetic and real indoor scenes with multiview imagery, room structures, object-centric descriptions, and metric spatial annotations. We further introduce observation-consistent supervision that aligns each target scene with the visual evidence available in its input views. Experiments on held-out \textsc{XScene} scenes, real indoor images, and out-of-distribution SpatialGen cases evaluate structured scene prediction, object grounding, and spatial refinement.

AI.tldr: Scenix is a sparse-view 3D scene reconstruction framework that predicts executable scene programs—a structured representation instantiable into editable 3D scenes—from a few uncalibrated RGB views, using perception-grounded asset instantiation and closed-loop spatial refinement, trained on a new dataset of ~110K synthetic and real indoor scenes.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D scene generation methods either rely on text input or require continuous visual inputs with additional priors such as human-annotated masks or accurate 3D layouts, making them labor-intensive and inapplicable to general sparse-view scenarios. A system is needed that can infer room structure, associate objects across incomplete observations, and recover globally consistent spatial configurations from sparse uncalibrated views.
AI.method: Scenix predicts executable scene programs from sparse views via perception-grounded asset instantiation and closed-loop spatial refinement. A new dataset (~110K synthetic and real indoor scenes) with multiview imagery, room structures, object-centric descriptions, and metric spatial annotations is constructed. Observation-consistent supervision aligns each target scene with visual evidence in the input views.
AI.result: Experiments on held-out XScene scenes, real indoor images, and out-of-distribution SpatialGen cases evaluate structured scene prediction, object grounding, and spatial refinement.
AI.conclusion: Scenix enables structured, editable 3D indoor scene reconstruction from sparse uncalibrated views without requiring text input or additional human-annotated priors, producing globally consistent spatial configurations grounded in the visual evidence.

title: Stable Curves, Unstable Items: Item-Level Scaling Heterogeneity in Video LLMs
summary: Aggregate scaling curves suggest that Video LLMs improve smoothly or saturate as visual budgets grow. We show that this view can conceal large, opposing changes at the item level. We represent each frozen model--item pair by its response trajectory under controlled visual budgets and derive matched-grid measures of configuration complementarity, harmful transitions, and text overwrite. Across five open Video LLMs from three architecture families, four multiple-choice benchmark splits, open-ended QA and summarization, and fixed-history dialogue generation, no single budget serves all items. On the four-model matched MCQA grid, item-level oracle headroom spans $8.8$--$18.9$ accuracy points and $12.5$--$25.5\%$ of items are correct at a lower budget but wrong at a higher one. Task-appropriate continuous metrics show the same complementarity beyond multiple choice: Token-F1 oracle gaps are $2.7$--$3.7$ score points on MLVU generation and $3.8$--$4.8$ points on AVSD current-turn generation, even when mean quality improves with budget. The effect persists across frame count, spatial resolution, sampling policy, temporal--spatial allocation, and independently executed raw-video and cached pipelines, with per-item rates and membership tracking protocol choices. A controlled sampling intervention recovers $29.0\%$ of terminal regressions, and a structured frame audit identifies several recurring evidence pathways. We release per-item trajectories, protocol provenance, derived annotations, and reproducible analysis code as an auditing artifact. A confidence cascade matches fixed-$128f$ accuracy while reducing average shared frame cost by $31.7\%$, illustrating one operational use of the response matrix.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the assumption that Video LLMs improve smoothly with more visual input (frames/resolution), showing that aggregate scaling curves conceal large item-level variability. Across multiple models, benchmarks, and tasks, no single visual budget serves all items—some items that are correct at lower budgets become wrong at higher ones. The authors introduce response-trajectory-based metrics (configuration complementarity, harmful transitions, text overwrite), an auditing artifact with per-item trajectories, and a confidence cascade that cuts frame cost by 31.7% while matching fixed-128f accuracy.
AI.motivation: Aggregate scaling curves create a misleading impression that Video LLMs improve smoothly with more visual budgets, hiding opposing item-level changes. Understanding per-item response trajectories is crucial for reliable evaluation and cost-efficient deployment, as no single budget is optimal for all items.
AI.method: The authors represent each frozen model-item pair by its response trajectory across controlled visual budgets. They derive matched-grid measures: configuration complementarity, harmful transitions, and text overwrite. They evaluate across five open Video LLMs (three architecture families), four multiple-choice benchmarks, open-ended QA, summarization, and fixed-history dialogue generation. They analyze protocol variations (frame count, spatial resolution, sampling policy, temporal-spatial allocation, raw-video vs. cached pipelines), apply a controlled sampling intervention, conduct a structured frame audit, and build a confidence cascade for cost reduction.
AI.result: No single budget serves all items. Item-level oracle headroom is 8.8-18.9 accuracy points on matched MCQA grid; 12.5-25.5% of items are correct at lower but wrong at higher budgets. Token-F1 oracle gaps are 2.7-3.7 on MLVU generation and 3.8-4.8 on AVSD even when mean quality improves. The confidence cascade matches fixed-128f accuracy while reducing average shared frame cost by 31.7%.
AI.conclusion: Aggregate scaling curves conceal significant per-item complementarity in Video LLMs. Item-level trajectory analysis is necessary for understanding model behavior, auditing failures, and enabling cost-efficient deployment. The released auditing artifact supports reproducible analysis and practical use (e.g., confidence cascade for frame-cost reduction).

title: Understand Before Detect: Vision--Language Learning for Omni-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection
summary: Omni-domain infrared small target (IRST) detection is crucial for infrared surveillance, yet remains challenging due to heterogeneous imaging domains and inconsistent target characteristics. Previous deep learning-based methods have been developed for visual-only paradigms and achieved promising performance on domain-specific tasks. However, existing methods follow the task-specific supervised learning paradigm. This paradigm simplifies the full-scene infrared observations to sparse target supervision, discarding the semantics that remain invariant across heterogeneous domains. Consequently, detection performance suffers substantially under domain shifts. To handle this issue, we introduce \textbf{``understand before detect''}, a paradigm that formulates omni-domain IRST detection as an understanding-driven process, where holistic infrared target understanding precedes precise detection. Building on this paradigm, we propose \textbf{JinSight}, which first develops holistic IRST understanding through language supervision and then transfers the learned cross-domain representations to precise small-target detection. By grounding infrared representations in language semantics, JinSight enables a single model to generalize across heterogeneous infrared domains. We then introduce Latent Semantic Interaction (LSI), which exchanges language-aligned global semantics with fine-grained spatial features in a compact low-rank space. To address the lack of multimodal omni-domain IRST benchmarks, we build \textbf{OmniIRST-VL}, the first large-scale, highly diverse vision--language dataset for omni-domain IRST detection. It comprises over 39k annotations across six complementary instruction tasks covering both scene-level understanding and target-centric reasoning.

AI.tldr: JinSight introduces an "understand before detect" paradigm for omni-domain infrared small target (IRST) detection, using language supervision to learn holistic infrared scene understanding before transferring these cross-domain representations to precise target detection. It also introduces OmniIRST-VL, the first large-scale vision-language dataset for omni-domain IRST detection with over 39k annotations across six instruction tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing deep learning methods for IRST detection follow task-specific supervised learning, which simplifies full-scene infrared observations to sparse target supervision and discards domain-invariant semantics. This causes substantial performance degradation under domain shifts across heterogeneous infrared imaging domains.
AI.method: JinSight proposes an "understand before detect" paradigm: (1) first develops holistic IRST understanding through language supervision, (2) transfers learned cross-domain representations to precise small-target detection, and (3) introduces Latent Semantic Interaction (LSI) to exchange language-aligned global semantics with fine-grained spatial features in a compact low-rank space. Additionally, OmniIRST-VL dataset is constructed with over 39k annotations across six instruction tasks covering scene-level understanding and target-centric reasoning.
AI.result: The paper presents the OmniIRST-VL benchmark, the first large-scale, highly diverse vision-language dataset for omni-domain IRST detection, enabling a single model to generalize across heterogeneous infrared domains through language-grounded representations.
AI.conclusion: By grounding infrared representations in language semantics and adopting an understanding-driven paradigm, JinSight enables a single model to generalize across heterogeneous infrared domains, addressing the domain-shift problem in omni-domain IRST detection.

title: YOLO-PEFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on YOLO Family
summary: Generic parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods transferred from language models can fail silently on real-time detectors, whose heterogeneous operators and detection-specific components impose placement constraints absent from regular Transformer stacks. We propose YOLO-PEFT, a structure-aware framework that formulates adapter placement as an auditable constraint-planning problem. Given a detector graph, a PEFT request, and a resource budget, YOLO-PEFT assigns operator and semantic roles, evaluates explicit operator-validity, detector-semantic, graph-interface, and deployment predicates, records a reason code for each excluded module, and either emits a budgeted target-module plan or returns Refuse before training. Under the official VOC07+12 trainval-to-VOC07 test protocol, planner-selected RS-LoRA reaches 0.7138 and 0.7307 mAP50-95 on YOLO11s and YOLO12s, respectively, compared with 0.6428 and 0.6662 for Full-SFT.
