title: Representation-driven Endoscopic Visual Embedding Alignment for Latent Generation
summary: Developing foundation generative models for endoscopy is limited by the gap between natural and clinical images and the computational cost of training large Diffusion Transformers. Although representation alignment has improved efficiency in general computer vision, its role within the highly specialized endoscopic image space remains unclear. We introduce REVEAL (Representation-driven Endoscopic Visual Embedding Alignment), the largest generative foundation model for endoscopy to date, trained on GastroNet-5M (GN-5M), a multicenter dataset of 5 million endoscopic frames. Instead of depending on out-of-domain priors, REVEAL employs encoders pretrained directly on the endoscopic distribution to align diffusion latents with domain-specific visual features, preserving fine textures and intricate anatomical structures. Beyond image generation, REVEAL also serves as a powerful feature extractor; in multiple benchmarks, it delivers performance that is competitive with, and in several cases exceeds, endoscopic foundation models such as EndoViT and Endo-FM, specifically tuned for classification tasks, while demonstrating strong representation robustness under realistic imaging corruptions. REVEAL produces high-fidelity images and maintains robust structural coherence in latent-space edits such as inpainting and outpainting. This high-capacity backbone lowers the computational threshold for building specialized clinical tools, offering an open, versatile foundation for conditional synthesis, segmentation, and out-of-distribution detection in future intelligent gastroenterology systems.

AI.tldr: REVEAL is the largest generative foundation model for endoscopy, trained on a 5-million-frame multicenter dataset (GastroNet-5M). It uses encoders pretrained on endoscopic images to align diffusion latents with domain-specific features, achieving high-fidelity generation while also serving as a powerful feature extractor competitive with or surpassing specialized endoscopic foundation models like EndoViT and Endo-FM.
AI.motivation: Developing foundation generative models for endoscopy is limited by (1) the gap between natural and clinical images, and (2) the high computational cost of training large Diffusion Transformers. The role of representation alignment within the specialized endoscopic image space remains unclear.
AI.method: REVEAL employs encoders pretrained directly on the endoscopic distribution to align diffusion latents with domain-specific visual features, avoiding reliance on out-of-domain priors and preserving fine textures and intricate anatomical structures.
AI.result: REVEAL delivers competitive or superior performance versus endoscopic foundation models (EndoViT, Endo-FM) on classification benchmarks, demonstrates strong representation robustness under realistic imaging corruptions, produces high-fidelity images, and maintains structural coherence in latent-space edits (inpainting/outpainting).
AI.conclusion: REVEAL lowers the computational threshold for building specialized clinical tools, offering an open, versatile foundation for conditional synthesis, segmentation, and out-of-distribution detection in future intelligent gastroenterology systems.

title: Flow-Corrected Shape Optimization: Taming Manifold Drift in High-Dimensional 3D Models
summary: Optimizing 3D shapes within the latent spaces of deep generative models is fundamental to computer assisted engineering, yet remains prone to a critical failure mode we term manifold drift: the tendency of gradient-based optimization to move latent vectors away from the manifold of valid shapes. This problem is exacerbated in state-of-the-art 3D shape generative models that operate in increasingly high-dimensional latent spaces where valid shapes occupy a vanishingly small fraction of the full space. Existing mitigation strategies, including latent regularization and flow-matching approaches, either sacrifice expressiveness, demand a difficult trade-off between objective guidance and generative fidelity that remains prone to manifold drift, or are computationally infeasible to scale to modern, large-capacity 3D shape models. We introduce a novel optimizer-corrector framework that alternates between gradient steps for objective minimization and guided flow matching to drive the latent state back to the valid shape manifold. By decoupling objective minimization from flow-based correction, optimizing freely and correcting strictly, this alternating design avoids inherent trade-offs, preserving geometric validity without sacrificing expressiveness while remaining computationally feasible on modern 3D shape models. We demonstrate its effectiveness across generative priors of varying complexity, from simple vector latent spaces to large-scale architectures across a variety of downstream optimization tasks, including aerodynamic drag reduction and object compliance optimization.

AI.tldr: A novel optimizer-corrector framework that alternates between gradient-based objective minimization and guided flow matching to keep latent vectors on the valid shape manifold, addressing the "manifold drift" problem in 3D shape optimization within deep generative model latent spaces.
AI.motivation: Gradient-based optimization of 3D shapes in generative latent spaces suffers from "manifold drift," where latent vectors move away from the manifold of valid shapes. This is particularly problematic in high-dimensional latent spaces where valid shapes occupy a tiny fraction of the space. Existing solutions either sacrifice expressiveness, face trade-offs between objective guidance and generative fidelity, or are computationally infeasible for large modern models.
AI.method: An alternating optimizer-corrector framework that decouples objective minimization from manifold correction: gradient steps minimize the objective function freely, while guided flow matching periodically drives the latent state back onto the valid shape manifold. This design avoids inherent trade-offs by separating the two concerns rather than combining them.
AI.result: Demonstrated effectiveness across generative priors of varying complexity—from simple vector latent spaces to large-scale architectures—on downstream optimization tasks including aerodynamic drag reduction and object compliance optimization.
AI.conclusion: The alternating optimizer-corrector approach preserves geometric validity without sacrificing expressiveness while remaining computationally feasible for modern 3D shape generation models, offering a scalable solution to manifold drift.

title: CANIS: Generation-Assisted 3D Canonicalization via an Image-Semantic Bridge
summary: Canonicalizing 3D object orientation is fundamental to 3D understanding and analysis. Existing approaches often rely on geometric cues, although 3D canonicalization ultimately requires a semantically meaningful orientation. To address this gap, we propose CANIS, a category-agnostic, generation-assisted framework that introduces the semantic orientation prior of a frozen image-to-3D generative model into 3D canonicalization, without canonicalization-specific training or category-specific templates. Specifically, CANIS first renders the input object from candidate viewpoints, selects an informative view, and generates a proxy in a canonical orientation. During generation, a sparse structural latent encoded from the input guides the proxy to preserve the geometry of an object. CANIS then uses the selected image as a semantic bridge between the input and the proxy. Image patches identify semantic regions on the proxy, and depth back-projection locates the corresponding regions on the input. The resulting semantic anchors constrain geometric matching, from which we estimate the rigid transformation that canonicalizes the input. Experiments on synthetic benchmarks validate CANIS and its key components, while qualitative results on partial observations and OmniObject3D suggest its applicability to incomplete and real-world scans. CANIS also improves downstream 3D classification, part segmentation, and dense correspondence under arbitrary rotations. Project page: https://kenkenzaii.github.io/Canis.

AI.tldr: CANIS is a category-agnostic framework that leverages semantic orientation priors from a frozen image-to-3D generative model to canonicalize 3D object orientation, without requiring canonicalization-specific training or category templates.
AI.motivation: Existing 3D canonicalization methods rely on geometric cues, but canonicalization fundamentally requires semantically meaningful orientation, which geometry alone cannot provide.
AI.method: CANIS renders the input object from candidate viewpoints, selects an informative view, generates a proxy in canonical orientation using a frozen image-to-3D generative model guided by a sparse structural latent, then uses the selected image as a semantic bridge—image patches identify semantic regions on the proxy and depth back-projection locates corresponding regions on the input, constraining geometric matching to estimate the rigid transformation for canonicalization.
AI.result: Experiments on synthetic benchmarks validate CANIS and its components; qualitative results on partial observations and OmniObject3D show applicability to incomplete and real-world scans. CANIS also improves downstream tasks including 3D classification, part segmentation, and dense correspondence under arbitrary rotations.
AI.conclusion: CANIS demonstrates that semantic priors from generative models can effectively address geometric-only limitations in 3D canonicalization, offering a generalizable solution across categories and real-world scenarios.

title: Foundation Models Adaptation for Multi-View Multi-modal Cardiac MRI Segmentation and Direct Ejection Fraction Estimation
summary: Foundation models have shown strong transferability in cardiac MRI (CMR), but their effectiveness for heterogeneous multi-view and multi-sequence CMR analysis remains unclear. In this work, we explore the effectiveness of fine-tuning and combining different CMR foundation models for the Universal Multi-Sequence, Multi-Center and Multi-View CMR Segmentation (CMR-Multi) Challenge. CineMA was fine-tuned for cine and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) segmentation across short-axis and long-axis views. For direct left-ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) estimation, we used two recent frozen CMR foundation models to extract embedding vectors that were then combined using attention-based multiple-instance learning for LVEF regression. In the challenge validation set, cine segmentation achieved Dice scores of 0.862, 0.883, and 0.902 for short-axis, two-chamber and four-chamber cine MRI, respectively. LGE segmentation achieved Dice scores between 0.621 and 0.846 across views. The direct LVEF regression model achieved an MAE of 4.96 percentage points and a Pearson correlation of 0.91. These results indicate that foundation models can be effectively adapted and combined for multi-view CMR analysis, while accurate LGE scar segmentation remains a challenging task.

AI.tldr: This paper explores fine-tuning and combining cardiac MRI foundation models for the CMR-Multi challenge, demonstrating effective adaptation of CineMA for multi-view cine/LGE segmentation and attention-based multiple-instance learning using frozen foundation model embeddings for direct LVEF regression.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether foundation models, which have shown strong transferability in cardiac MRI, can be effectively adapted and combined for heterogeneous multi-view and multi-sequence CMR analysis—a capability that remains unclear.
AI.method: Two approaches: (1) fine-tuning CineMA for cine and LGE segmentation across short-axis and long-axis views; (2) using two frozen CMR foundation models to extract embeddings, combined via attention-based multiple-instance learning for direct LVEF regression.
AI.result: Cine segmentation Dice scores of 0.862 (short-axis), 0.883 (2-chamber), 0.902 (4-chamber); LGE segmentation Dice 0.621-0.846 across views; LVEF regression achieved MAE of 4.96 percentage points and Pearson correlation of 0.91.
AI.conclusion: Foundation models can be effectively adapted and combined for multi-view CMR analysis, though accurate LGE scar segmentation remains a challenging task.

title: EliSeg: Verified Target Construction for Report-Grounded Abnormality Segmentation
summary: Radiology reports describe clinical observations but do not specify executable segmentation targets. They may contain present, negated, prior,uncertain, or irrelevant findings, while multiple valid abnormalities may coexist. Existing segmentation methods largely bypass this ambiguity by receiving a target identity or spatial prompt before inference, which acts as a hidden target oracle. We study report-grounded abnormality segmentation, where a model must determine target eligibility, cardinality, and finding-to-mask correspondence directly from an unfiltered report before delineating the corresponding regions. We propose \textbf{EliSeg}, an atcor--verify--revise framework that integrates target construction with mask generation. A grammar-constrained Actor proposes target slots and masks, an independent text-only Verifier reconstructs the eligible finding inventory, and Revision selectively re-executes the shared Actor when their target structures disagree. EliSeg requires no predefined target identity, finding prompt, point, or bounding box. Experiments on MIMIC-CXR-ILS show that EliSeg consistently outperforms direct segmentation methods and extract-then-segment cascades across findings, while effectively suppressing masks for ineligible report mentions. Ablation studies confirm the complementary roles of verification and revision, and evaluation on CheXlocalize demonstrates effective transfer of the EliSeg to an external dataset.Code is available at https://github.com/Maybach-dream/EliSeg.

AI.tldr: EliSeg is an actor-verify-revise framework for report-grounded abnormality segmentation that determines target eligibility, cardinality, and finding-to-mask correspondence directly from unfiltered radiology reports without any predefined target prompts or oracles, outperforming existing methods on MIMIC-CXR-ILS and transferring effectively to CheXlocalize.
AI.motivation: Existing segmentation methods bypass the inherent ambiguity of radiology reports by receiving a target identity or spatial prompt before inference (a hidden target oracle). Real-world reports contain present, negated, prior, uncertain, or irrelevant findings, and multiple abnormalities may coexist. A model must resolve target eligibility, cardinality, and finding-to-mask correspondence directly from an unfiltered report, which current approaches fail to address.
AI.method: EliSeg employs an actor-verify-revise framework. A grammar-constrained Actor proposes target slots and masks. An independent text-only Verifier reconstructs the eligible finding inventory. When the Actor's and Verifier's target structures disagree, a Revision step selectively re-executes the shared Actor. No predefined target identity, finding prompt, point, or bounding box is required.
AI.result: On MIMIC-CXR-ILS, EliSeg consistently outperforms direct segmentation methods and extract-then-segment cascades across findings while effectively suppressing masks for ineligible report mentions. Ablation studies confirm the complementary roles of verification and revision. Evaluation on CheXlocalize demonstrates effective transfer to an external dataset.
AI.conclusion: EliSeg demonstrates that ambiguity resolution and segmentation can be integrated into a single framework without target oracles, achieving superior performance and robust generalization to external datasets, with code publicly available.

title: Same Attention, Different Truths: Put Logit-Lens over Visual Attention to Detect and Mitigate LVLM Object Hallucination
summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) often suffer from object hallucination, generating objects that are absent from the image. Prior work largely attributes this to insufficient visual attention. However, we find that both real and hallucinated objects receive equally strong visual attention in the model's mid-to-late layers, suggesting that the key issue may not be how much the model attends, but what it attends to and why. To this end, we decode the visual features of high-attention regions using Logit Lens, and observe that regions corresponding to real objects can be correctly decoded to the target object tokens, whereas those for hallucinated objects cannot. Building on this, we identify two hallucination mechanisms: (i) visual uncertainty, triggered by semantically similar or confusable regions; masking these regions eliminates the hallucination. (ii) contextual prior, triggered by strong co-occurrence priors; even when the initially attended region is masked, the hallucination persists and attention drifts to other regions. Based on these findings, we propose a simple yet effective training-free Detect-Mitigate framework comprising a Logit-Lens Consistency Check to detect hallucination and targeted remedies: High-Attention Regions Masking (HARM) for visual uncertainty hallucination, and Visual Evidence Enhanced Decoding (VEED) for contextual prior hallucination. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple hallucination benchmarks. Code will be available.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates object hallucination in LVLMs, revealing that both real and hallucinated objects receive equally strong visual attention. By decoding visual features with Logit Lens, the authors identify two distinct hallucination mechanisms (visual uncertainty and contextual prior) and propose a training-free Detect-Mitigate framework that achieves state-of-the-art results on hallucination benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Prior work attributes object hallucination in LVLMs to insufficient visual attention, but the authors find this explanation incomplete—both real and hallucinated objects receive equally strong visual attention. This motivates a deeper investigation into what the model attends to and why, rather than how much it attends.
AI.method: The authors use Logit Lens to decode visual features of high-attention regions, identifying two hallucination mechanisms: (i) visual uncertainty from semantically similar/confusable regions, and (ii) contextual prior from strong co-occurrence priors. They propose a Detect-Mitigate framework with a Logit-Lens Consistency Check for detection, plus two targeted remedies: High-Attention Regions Masking (HARM) for visual uncertainty and Visual Evidence Enhanced Decoding (VEED) for contextual prior hallucination.
AI.result: The proposed training-free framework achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple hallucination benchmarks, demonstrating that targeted mitigation based on the underlying mechanism outperforms general-purpose approaches.
AI.conclusion: Object hallucination in LVLMs stems from two distinct mechanisms rather than simply insufficient attention. Understanding and diagnosing the specific failure mode enables effective, training-free mitigation that surpasses existing methods on hallucination benchmarks.

title: H2AL: Hyperbolic Hierarchy-aware Aggregative Learning for Registration-based Few-shot Medical Image Segmentation
comment: 10 pages, 9 figures. Accepted at ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26)
summary: Registration-based Few-shot medical image segmentation (RFMIS) aims to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled images by warping a labeled image through registration. However, existing methods primarily perform pixel-level optimization and inference in Euclidean space, treating anatomical structures as flat and disjoint. This neglect of inherent hierarchies degrades pseudo-label quality and weakens the discrimination of ambiguous regions, limiting the segmentation performance. To overcome this challenge, we propose a Hyperbolic Hierarchy-aware Aggregative Learning framework for RFMIS, termed H2AL, that enhances both deformation plausibility and anatomical discrimination for dual-task learning. Specifically, we introduce a Hyperbolic Hierarchy-aware Infusion (H2I) module, which leverages the hierarchical modeling capability of hyperbolic space to learn precise hierarchy-aware representations via transformation-guided supervised hyperbolic contrastive learning, and injects such hierarchical priors into Euclidean space through a gated infusion block while preserving semantic richness. Furthermore, we propose an end-to-end joint optimization algorithm by gradient aggregation, where the gradients from the registration and segmentation decoders, embedding semantic and hierarchical cues, are aggregated to update the shared encoder to promote collaborative learning across tasks. Extensive experiments on two anatomical regions, with five experimental settings, demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method in both registration and segmentation. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/JiamingCai469/H2AL.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes H2AL, a Hyperbolic Hierarchy-aware Aggregative Learning framework for registration-based few-shot medical image segmentation, which uses hyperbolic space to model anatomical hierarchies and a gradient-aggregation joint optimization to improve both registration and segmentation.
AI.motivation: Existing RFMIS methods perform optimization in Euclidean space, treating anatomical structures as flat and disjoint, which neglects inherent hierarchies and degrades pseudo-label quality and discrimination of ambiguous regions.
AI.method: H2AL introduces a Hyperbolic Hierarchy-aware Infusion (H2I) module that uses hyperbolic space for hierarchy-aware representation learning via transformation-guided supervised hyperbolic contrastive learning, then injects hierarchical priors into Euclidean space with a gated infusion block. An end-to-end joint optimization via gradient aggregation updates the shared encoder with gradients from both registration and segmentation decoders.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on two anatomical regions with five experimental settings demonstrate effectiveness and efficiency in both registration and segmentation tasks.
AI.conclusion: Modeling anatomical hierarchies in hyperbolic space and aggregating gradients across dual tasks improves deformation plausibility and anatomical discrimination in RFMIS.

title: SkySeaLand: A Wide-Format Satellite Transportation Benchmark with an Ultra-Lightweight Detection Baseline
summary: Satellite object detection is challenged by small targets and wide-format scenes that lose detail under standard square-input resizing. We introduce SkySeaLand, a public dataset of 1,307 high-resolution satellite images and 19,101 verified bounding boxes across airplane, boat, car, and ship classes in terrestrial and maritime scenes. Native COCO and YOLO annotations are provided. The collection is dominated by large source images and wide scene geometry: 84.5 percent exceed 3,836 pixels on the longest side and 73.1 percent are near a 3:1 aspect ratio. We evaluate twelve detectors from the YOLO, RT-DETR, DETR, and Faster R-CNN families using a common split and COCO metrics. The tested YOLO and RT-DETR variants obtain 84.4--88.2 mAP50, with no consistent accuracy gain from larger parameter counts under the reported model-specific recipes. We also report SkyDet, a 1.22 M parameter anchor-free baseline that obtains 60.5 mAP50 and 24.32 mAP50-95 in a 4.90 MB footprint, with 13.74 ms latency (72.8 FPS) on a Tesla T4. SkySeaLand provides a compact benchmark for mixed land--maritime transportation detection, while SkyDet establishes a documented low-footprint reference rather than a state-of-the-art accuracy claim.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces SkySeaLand, a benchmark dataset of 1,307 high-resolution satellite images with 19,101 bounding boxes across four transportation classes (airplane, boat, car, ship) in terrestrial and maritime scenes, featuring wide-format geometry (73.1% near 3:1 aspect ratio) and large source images (84.5% exceed 3,836 pixels). The authors evaluate twelve detectors from YOLO, RT-DETR, DETR, and Faster R-CNN families, finding YOLO and RT-DETR variants achieve 84.4-88.2 mAP50 with no consistent gain from larger models. They also present SkyDet, a compact 1.22M-parameter baseline achieving 60.5 mAP50 with only 4.90 MB footprint and 72.8 FPS.
AI.motivation: Satellite object detection faces challenges with small targets and wide-format scenes because standard square-input resizing loses critical detail. Existing datasets and evaluation protocols do not adequately address wide-format scene geometry, motivating the need for a dedicated benchmark and lightweight baseline suitable for this domain.
AI.method: The authors construct SkySeaLand, a dataset of 1,307 high-resolution satellite images with 19,101 verified bounding boxes annotated in native COCO and YOLO formats. They systematically evaluate twelve detectors spanning YOLO, RT-DETR, DETR, and Faster R-CNN families using a common train/val split and COCO metrics. They additionally develop SkyDet, a compact 1.22M parameter anchor-free detector, and report its accuracy, footprint, and latency.
AI.result: YOLO and RT-DETR variants achieve 84.4-88.2 mAP50 with no consistent accuracy improvement from larger parameter counts under the reported recipes. SkyDet achieves 60.5 mAP50 and 24.32 mAP50-95 with a 4.90 MB footprint and 13.74 ms latency (72.8 FPS) on a Tesla T4.
AI.conclusion: SkySeaLand serves as a compact benchmark for mixed land-maritime transportation detection, addressing the under-represented wide-format satellite imagery scenario. SkyDet establishes a documented low-footprint reference baseline rather than claiming state-of-the-art accuracy, highlighting the trade-off between model size and performance in this setting.

title: GeoDistill-Refine: Silhouette-First Geometry Distillation for Annotation-Free Spacecraft Segmentation
summary: Foundation segmentation models can provide supervision for spacecraft imagery without manual training masks, but their predictions vary with textual prompts and may contain geometric errors that are amplified during distillation. This paper presents GeoDistill-Refine, a two-stage framework that transfers offline SAM 3 pseudo-masks to a compact segmentation network. Six fixed prompts are fused by an unweighted 50% vote to stabilize the teacher output. The student first learns the foreground silhouette and is then refined with signed-distance-field, skeleton, and area objectives derived from the pseudo-mask. A sample-level gate, computed from prompt agreement, the valid-prompt ratio, and pseudo-mask area plausibility, reduces the influence of unreliable pseudo-geometry. On the SpaceSense-Bench HJM lockbox set, GeoDistill-Refine improves Image IoU and Boundary F1 by 0.0456 and 0.1380, respectively, over a plain pseudo-label student. External evaluations on the SPEED+ Lightbox and Sunlamp domains and on TANGO show competitive regional overlap together with gains in boundary quality or foreground precision. The deployed TinyUNet contains 0.263 M parameters and requires approximately 1.1 ms per image on an RTX 4090; SAM 3 pseudo-mask construction and the auxiliary geometry branches are used only during training.

AI.tldr: GeoDistill-Refine is a two-stage knowledge distillation framework that transfers SAM 3 pseudo-masks to a compact TinyUNet (0.263M params) for spacecraft image segmentation, using prompt-voting, geometric auxiliary objectives (signed-distance-field, skeleton, area), and a sample-level reliability gate, achieving gains of +0.0456 Image IoU and +0.1380 Boundary F1 over a plain pseudo-label student.
AI.motivation: Foundation segmentation models (e.g., SAM 3) can supervise spacecraft imagery without manual masks, but their predictions are sensitive to text prompts and contain geometric errors that get amplified during distillation.
AI.method: A two-stage framework: (1) six fixed prompts fused by unweighted 50% vote to stabilize SAM 3 teacher outputs; (2) a student first learns the foreground silhouette, then is refined with signed-distance-field, skeleton, and area objectives derived from pseudo-masks. A sample-level gate using prompt agreement, valid-prompt ratio, and pseudo-mask area plausibility down-weights unreliable pseudo-geometry.
AI.result: On SpaceSense-Bench HJM lockbox, improves Image IoU by 0.0456 and Boundary F1 by 0.1380 over a plain pseudo-label student. External evaluations on SPEED+ Lightbox, Sunlamp, and TANGO show competitive IoU with gains in boundary quality or foreground precision. Deployed TinyUNet: 0.263M params, ~1.1 ms/image on RTX 4090.
AI.conclusion: Offline geometric refinement and reliability gating enable compact students to distill noisy foundation-model pseudo-masks with superior boundary quality, while keeping heavy teacher computation entirely offline (inference-time cost stays minimal).

title: Addressable Memory for Video World Models
summary: We study visual persistence in interactive video world models. These models rely on a Key-Value (KV) cache as a growing visual memory to carry forward previously generated frames. However, we find that models can no longer reliably address stored content once rollouts extend beyond the training horizon, because temporal Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE) offsets then fall outside the range seen during training and the model struggles to retrieve the relevant visual information through attention. Moreover, naively compressing the cache in the RoPE-rotated space corrupts memory by averaging together incompatible positional phases. To address this, we propose WorldTrace, a training-free memory framework for long-horizon visual persistence. WorldTrace keeps compressed memory addressable by assigning each summary slot a distinct, in-distribution virtual position. Within this addressable cache, we study two memory compression approaches: WorldTrace-Field compresses history for temporal coherence, while WorldTrace-Landmark stores verbatim scene traces at detected transitions for episodic recall. We further introduce LoopBench, a benchmark evaluating whether a compressed cache can reconstruct a previously visited scene after a long detour. WorldTrace-Field improves temporal consistency by +15.5%, and WorldTrace-Landmark improves episodic recall by +19.5% on LoopBench, extending visually persistent generation without retraining.

AI.tldr: WorldTrace is a training-free memory framework that addresses visual persistence failures in interactive video world models by keeping compressed KV-cache memory addressable through in-distribution virtual positions, with two compression approaches (Field for temporal coherence, Landmark for episodic recall), validated on a new LoopBench benchmark.
AI.motivation: Interactive video world models use a growing KV cache as visual memory, but fail to retrieve stored content during long rollouts because temporal RoPE offsets exceed the training range, and naively compressing the cache in RoPE-rotated space corrupts memory by averaging incompatible positional phases.
AI.method: WorldTrace assigns each compressed memory summary slot a distinct, in-distribution virtual position to keep it addressable outside the training horizon. It proposes two compression strategies: WorldTrace-Field compresses history for temporal coherence, and WorldTrace-Landmark stores verbatim scene traces at detected transitions for episodic recall. A new benchmark, LoopBench, evaluates whether a compressed cache can reconstruct a previously visited scene after a long detour.
AI.result: WorldTrace-Field improves temporal consistency by +15.5% and WorldTrace-Landmark improves episodic recall by +19.5% on LoopBench, extending visually persistent generation without retraining.
AI.conclusion: The proposed training-free memory framework successfully addresses the positional embedding out-of-distribution problem and cache compression corruption, enabling long-horizon visual persistence in interactive video world models without retraining.

title: UniJEPA: A Unified Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Task-Agnostic Visual World Modeling
summary: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) have emerged as a principled framework for self-supervised learning of world models in compact latent spaces, yet existing methods are fragmented: some predict masked parts of a single image in latent space (I-JEPA), others learn to predict global photometric transformations (Image World Models), while video-scale JEPAs predict future temporal states and are post-trained for action-conditioned planning (V-JEPA~2, DINO-World, DINO-WM). These objectives are treated as distinct recipes with separate encoders, predictors, and anti-collapse regularizers, hindering a single model from unifying image-level and video-level world modeling. We present UniJEPA, a unified JEPA that jointly learns photometric prediction (image-level transformations) and temporal prediction (video-level next-state dynamics) in one shared latent space. A single end-to-end objective, composed of a next-embedding prediction loss and a Gaussian regularizer, yields a provably anti-collapse encoder-predictor pair trainable from raw pixels without EMA, stop-gradient, or pre-trained encoders. We show that the same latent space supports controllable abstraction: photometric prediction learns invariant structure while temporal prediction learns equivariant dynamics. After action-conditioned post-training on offline trajectories, UniJEPA enables zero-shot planning by treating goal features as prediction targets. On image, video, and control benchmarks, UniJEPA matches or surpasses task-specific JEPAs while requiring a single loss hyperparameter, and plans up to tens of times faster than generative world models at comparable accuracy.

AI.tldr: UniJEPA is a unified Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture that jointly learns photometric (image-level) and temporal (video-level) predictions in one shared latent space with a single end-to-end objective, achieving controllable abstraction (invariant structure + equivariant dynamics) and enabling fast zero-shot planning after action-conditioned post-training.
AI.motivation: Existing JEPA variants are fragmented—treating image-level and video-level world modeling as distinct recipes with separate encoders, predictors, and anti-collapse regularizers—hindering a single model from unifying both levels of world modeling.
AI.method: UniJEPA uses a single end-to-end objective comprising a next-embedding prediction loss and a Gaussian regularizer, which provably prevents collapse without EMA, stop-gradient, or pre-trained encoders. A shared latent space supports both photometric prediction (invariant structure) and temporal prediction (equivariant dynamics), with action-conditioned post-training enabling planning by using goal features as prediction targets.
AI.result: UniJEPA matches or surpasses task-specific JEPAs on image, video, and control benchmarks with only a single loss hyperparameter, and plans up to tens of times faster than generative world models at comparable accuracy.
AI.conclusion: A unified JEPA framework can jointly learn image-level and video-level world modeling in one shared latent space, demonstrating that unified JEPA training is not only feasible but also competitive with and often superior to task-specialized alternatives, with significant computational advantages for planning.

title: I Seek You in Videos: Identity-Conditioned Queries for Person-Centric Video Reasoning
comment: Accepted to ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26). 6 figures, 5 tables
summary: Real-world video reasoning often involves multimodal, multi-source inputs, whereas existing video reasoning tasks typically assume a simplified video-text setting, limiting identity matching and person-centric reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Identity-conditioned Queries (ICQ) task, in which models are required to jointly associate and interpret an input video and a reference image of a person, and leverage this conditioning to address identity grounding, behavior understanding, and temporal reasoning, among other challenges. Building on ICQ, we present ISYV (I Seek You in Videos), a systematic solution comprising three components: (1) ISYV-Bench, a challenging evaluation benchmark with 1,377 real-world complex videos and 1,377 question-answer pairs, organized into six difficulty levels spanning capabilities from identity recognition to causal reasoning; (2) ISYV-75K, a large-scale training set of 75K high-quality samples constructed via automated annotation, multi-stage verification, and manual review; and (3) ISYV-Framework, containing an ICQ-oriented model and training strategy for learning to exploit informative video shots without additional shot-level annotations. Extensive experiments show that both mainstream closed-source and open-source MLLMs struggle on ISYV-Bench, especially in cross-domain identity matching and long-horizon tracking. ISYV-Model outperforms strong baselines and in some aspects approaches closed-source performance. Overall, ISYV provides a unified task definition, scalable datasets/benchmarks, and modeling insights for person-centric video reasoning.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Identity-conditioned Queries (ICQ), a new task requiring models to jointly interpret videos and reference images of specific people for person-centric reasoning. The authors present ISYV, a complete solution including a benchmark (ISYV-Bench with 1,377 videos/QAs across six difficulty levels), a large training dataset (ISYV-75K), and a framework (ISYV-Framework) with an ICQ-oriented model and training strategy. Experiments show mainstream MLLMs struggle on this task, while ISYV-Model outperforms baselines and approaches closed-source performance in some aspects.
AI.motivation: Existing video reasoning tasks assume a simplified video-text setting, which limits identity matching and person-centric reasoning. Real-world video reasoning often involves multimodal, multi-source inputs (e.g., a reference image of a person alongside a video), but current benchmarks and models do not support this more realistic scenario.
AI.method: ISYV comprises three components: (1) ISYV-Bench, a benchmark with 1,377 real-world videos and QA pairs organized into six difficulty levels spanning from identity recognition to causal reasoning; (2) ISYV-75K, a large-scale training set of 75K high-quality samples built via automated annotation, multi-stage verification, and manual review; (3) ISYV-Framework, containing an ICQ-oriented model and training strategy that learns to exploit informative video shots without needing shot-level annotations.
AI.result: Experiments show that both mainstream closed-source and open-source MLLMs struggle on ISYV-Bench, particularly on cross-domain identity matching and long-horizon tracking. ISYV-Model outperforms strong baselines and approaches closed-source performance in some aspects.
AI.conclusion: ISYV provides a unified task definition, scalable datasets/benchmarks, and modeling insights for person-centric video reasoning, addressing the gap between simplified video-text settings and real-world multimodal reasoning requirements.

title: Conformal Coverage Guarantees for Any Video Temporal Grounder
summary: Event boundaries in continuous video are ambiguous: re-annotate the same query-video pair and independent annotators mark moments that overlap by less than half on a large fraction of samples. The ground truth for video temporal grounding is therefore a distribution over intervals, yet every grounder returns a single interval with no statement of reliability, so at deployment a wrong interval is indistinguishable from a right one. COVER changes the output object: a post-hoc, model-agnostic wrapper that turns any grounder, a trained localizer or a black-box video--language model, into one that emits a temporal region containing the true moment with probability at least $1-α$, by calibrating the quantile of a temporal nonconformity score on held-out labels and widening the base prediction by that amount. The guarantee is finite-sample and distribution-free under exchangeability, and requires neither retraining nor white-box access. We give two score families, a two-sided boundary-widening score for grounders that emit an interval and a super-level-set score for grounders that emit a relevance signal, and develop theory specific to grounding that bounds how large the certified region becomes, when coverage survives conditioning on event length, and how it degrades when moments from one video break exchangeability. Across three benchmarks and five grounders, realized coverage tracks the target, and calibration exposes what point metrics hide.

AI.tldr: COVER is a post-hoc, model-agnostic wrapper that converts any video temporal grounding model into one that outputs a certified temporal region containing the true moment with probability at least 1-α, using conformal prediction.
AI.motivation: Event boundaries in continuous video are ambiguous, so ground truth for video temporal grounding is a distribution over intervals. Yet existing grounders return a single interval with no reliability statement, making wrong predictions indistinguishable from correct ones at deployment.
AI.method: COVER calibrates the quantile of a temporal nonconformity score on held-out labels and widens the base prediction accordingly. It provides two score families: a two-sided boundary-widening score for interval-emitting grounders and a super-level-set score for relevance-signal-emitting grounders. It requires no retraining or white-box access and provides finite-sample, distribution-free guarantees under exchangeability.
AI.result: Across three benchmarks and five grounders, realized coverage tracks the target, and calibration exposes what point metrics hide. The method also includes theory bounding certified region size, coverage conditioning on event length, and degradation when moments from one video break exchangeability.
AI.conclusion: COVER provides reliable uncertainty quantification for video temporal grounding by outputting calibrated temporal regions instead of point intervals, with finite-sample coverage guarantees applicable to any existing grounder.

title: SABRE: Scalable and Automated Benchmarking of VLMs under Stress
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures. Code and resources will be available at https://zesearch.github.io/vlm-SABRE/
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are improving rapidly, but benchmark development lags behind, making weaknesses hard to identify. Building stress tests is costly: samples must satisfy controlled conditions, remain answerable, and challenge current models. We present SABRE, a scalable, automated pipeline that converts a Test Primer (a Markdown Task Design with Data Schema) into structured specifications, generated or edited images, and question-answer pairs. Automated filtering removes candidates solved by a Filtering VLM, while human review verifies candidate validity and supports annotation correction and localized image repair. We instantiate SABRE-Prior to test whether VLMs follow visual evidence instead of relying on world priors -- learned expectations about familiar objects and scenes. Its 600 images and 1,000 questions span Context (unexpected entities in familiar scenes), Texture (counterfactual materials), Attribute (noncanonical component counts), and Language Elicitation (answers suggested by language but unsupported by the image). Across six VLMs, macro-average accuracy ranges from 17.8% to 31.3% (22.6% mean). A real-image Attribute control is comparably difficult for the Filtering VLM. SABRE-Counting and SABRE-Spatial pilots show that the workflow supports other stress-test settings. These results establish SABRE as a reusable framework for constructing and refreshing VLM stress tests rather than a single fixed benchmark.

AI.tldr: SABRE is a scalable, automated pipeline for generating VLM stress tests, demonstrated through SABRE-Prior which tests whether VLMs follow visual evidence over world priors, achieving only 17.8-31.3% accuracy across six VLMs.
AI.motivation: Benchmark development for VLMs lags behind model improvements, and building stress tests is costly because samples must satisfy controlled conditions, remain answerable, and challenge current models.
AI.method: SABRE converts a Test Primer (Markdown Task Design with Data Schema) into structured specifications, generated/edited images, and QA pairs. Automated filtering removes candidates solved by a Filtering VLM, and human review verifies validity with annotation correction and localized image repair. SABRE-Prior tests vision priors across Context, Texture, Attribute, and Language Elicitation categories.
AI.result: SABRE-Prior contains 600 images and 1,000 questions. Across six VLMs, macro-average accuracy ranges from 17.8% to 31.3% (22.6% mean). A real-image Attribute control is comparably difficult for the Filtering VLM. SABRE-Counting and SABRE-Spatial pilots confirm the workflow generalizes to other stress-test settings.
AI.conclusion: SABRE is a reusable framework for constructing and refreshing VLM stress tests rather than a single fixed benchmark, demonstrating that current VLMs struggle to follow visual evidence over world priors.

title: MirrorWorld: Taming Video Diffusion Models for Mirror Reflection Generation
summary: Recent advances in video diffusion models (VDMs) have enabled high-fidelity video synthesis. However, generating mirror reflections remains challenging because the content within a mirror must remain consistent with the surrounding scene. Existing VDMs are not specifically designed to model scene-to-mirror relationships, which can lead to reflections with incorrect content or inconsistent spatial arrangements. We observe that mirror reflection generation involves two complementary challenges: determining what scene content should be reflected and how the reflected content should be spatially arranged within the mirror region. Motivated by this observation, we propose MirrorWorld, a reflection-aware video inpainting framework that models scene-to-mirror relationships during generation. Specifically, we introduce Semantic Relation Distillation (SRD), which transfers relational information from a frozen visual foundation model to encourage semantic associations between visible scene content and mirror regions. We further propose Geometric Transformation Alignment (GTA), which learns a transformation that guides the spatial arrangement of reflected content. The two components play complementary roles, with SRD modeling what should be reflected and GTA modeling how it should be arranged. To facilitate research on this problem, we construct a benchmark for video mirror reflection generation by repurposing four existing video mirror datasets into a unified reflection reconstruction task. Experimental results show that MirrorWorld achieves improved reflection reconstruction quality over representative image-based reflection generation methods and strong video inpainting baselines.

AI.tldr: MirrorWorld is a reflection-aware video inpainting framework that models scene-to-mirror relationships using two complementary components: Semantic Relation Distillation (SRD) for determining what content should be reflected, and Geometric Transformation Alignment (GTA) for spatial arrangement of reflections. It also introduces a unified benchmark for video mirror reflection generation.
AI.motivation: Video diffusion models struggle with mirror reflection generation because existing VDMs are not designed to model scene-to-mirror relationships, leading to reflections with incorrect content or inconsistent spatial arrangements. The problem decomposes into two challenges: what scene content should be reflected and how it should be spatially arranged within the mirror region.
AI.method: MirrorWorld proposes a reflection-aware video inpainting framework with two key components: (1) Semantic Relation Distillation (SRD) that transfers relational information from a frozen visual foundation model to encourage semantic associations between visible scene content and mirror regions; (2) Geometric Transformation Alignment (GTA) that learns a transformation guiding the spatial arrangement of reflected content. A unified benchmark is constructed by repurposing four existing video mirror datasets into a unified reflection reconstruction task.
AI.result: Experimental results show that MirrorWorld achieves improved reflection reconstruction quality over representative image-based reflection generation methods and strong video inpainting baselines.
AI.conclusion: MirrorWorld effectively models scene-to-mirror relationships in video generation by separating the reflection problem into semantic (what) and geometric (how) components, demonstrating superior performance on the newly constructed unified benchmark.

title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
comment: The code and model weights are available at https://github.com/H-EmbodVis/SimWAM/
summary: World-Action Models (WAMs) improve end-to-end autonomous driving by transferring video dynamics priors to action prediction, but existing methods require costly future generation at inference. We present SimWAM, a simple yet effective WAM that uses video generation purely as a training signal. It co-trains a pretrained video expert and a lightweight action expert with joint flow matching. An isolated attention mask keeps action prediction independent of future frames, allowing the video branch to be discarded after training and leaving a self-contained planner that directly predicts trajectories. Since the two experts share no parameters and interact only through a unified attention interface, the video backbone could be replaced and the action expert scaled independently without modifying the learning objective or inference pipeline. We further apply reinforcement learning to optimize a compositional driving reward beyond trajectory imitation. Our SimWAM achieves $91.5$ PDMS on NAVSIM, surpasses state-of-the-art WAM-based planners with substantially lower latency, and transfers zero-shot to nuScenes. These results position SimWAM as a simple yet solid baseline that could readily benefit from advances in video generation for efficient autonomous driving. The code and model weights are available at https://github.com/H-EmbodVis/SimWAM/

AI.tldr: SimWAM is a simple yet effective World-Action Model that uses video generation purely as a training signal via joint flow matching between a pretrained video expert and a lightweight action expert, enabling the video branch to be discarded after training. It achieves 91.5 PDMS on NAVSIM with lower latency than existing WAM planners and transfers zero-shot to nuScenes.
AI.motivation: Existing World-Action Models (WAMs) improve end-to-end autonomous driving by leveraging video dynamics priors, but they require costly future frame generation at inference time, which is computationally expensive and impractical for real-time driving.
AI.method: SimWAM co-trains a pretrained video expert and a lightweight action expert using joint flow matching. An isolated attention mask keeps action prediction independent of future frames, allowing the video branch to be discarded after training. The two experts share no parameters and interact only through a unified attention interface, enabling interchangeable backbones and scalable action experts. Reinforcement learning is applied to optimize a compositional driving reward beyond trajectory imitation.
AI.result: SimWAM achieves 91.5 PDMS on NAVSIM, surpassing state-of-the-art WAM-based planners with substantially lower latency, and transfers zero-shot to nuScenes.
AI.conclusion: SimWAM serves as a simple yet solid baseline that can readily benefit from advances in video generation while delivering efficient, self-contained trajectory planning for autonomous driving.
